functions.funcDef: Produce propulsive thrust for all phases of flight from four podded turbofans (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans on the high wing produce thrust for all flight phases (§5.1.1); in: fuel at pump inlet, throttle commands; out: thrust, engine-parameter data to AVI.

functions.funcDef: Produce propulsive thrust for all phases of flight from four podded turbofans (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide ground deceleration by reverse thrust
functions.subDef: Thrust reversers on the two inboard engines provide reverse thrust on the ground, inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement (§5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subName: Control aircraft attitude about three axes
functions.subDef: Position primary surfaces — ailerons/spoilers (roll), stabiliser/elevators (pitch), split rudder (yaw) — in response to pilot and autopilot commands (§5.3.1–5.3.2); in: HYD A/B/C, inceptor, air/inertial data; out: surface position/status to AVI.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Extend/retract double-slotted Fowler flaps (four sections) and full-span slats via two independent power drive units on a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2); out: high-lift position to performance computation.

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground and provide deceleration and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Nose unit and six main bogies support the aircraft, absorb landing/taxi loads and spread footprint pressure to the flotation the semi-prepared surface demands; retract/extend by HYD A with free-fall alternate (§5.6.1–5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground and provide deceleration and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Decelerate aircraft on the ground by wheel braking
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking, normally HYD B alternately HYD A with accumulator emergency reserve and per-wheel-pair anti-skid (§5.6.2); sizing case is the 1,800 m landing requirement (§5.6.3).

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground and provide deceleration and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Provide ground directional control by nose-wheel steering
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access to the full hold length and confirm secure closure of the nose door (SDD §5.7.1).
functions.subName: Open and close nose cargo door
functions.subDef: Upward-hinging nose visor opened/closed hydraulically from HYD A with electric backup, operable only on the ground (§5.7.2, §5.7.6).

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access to the full hold length and confirm secure closure of the nose door (SDD §5.7.1).
functions.subName: Secure and monitor nose door locking
functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches plus eight independent locking pins on a separate supply, dual dissimilar lock sensing, and a pressure interlock in series with unlock (§5.7.2–5.7.3); out: lock status to flight deck and take-off config monitor.

functions.funcDef: Position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases and monitor restraint (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subName: Restrain payload against flight and ground loads
functions.subDef: Nine saddles with two tension straps each (electric winch, mechanically locked); saddle geometry provides lateral/vertical restraint; loss of any one strap carried by neighbours (§5.8.2–5.8.3).

functions.funcDef: Position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases and monitor restraint (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Single instrumented tension loop reads every strap continuously; loss of tension annunciated in flight, adjacent-station loss annunciated as a restraint condition (§5.8.2); out: restraint status to take-off config monitor.

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two air-cycle packs fed from four engine bleeds through a cross-bleed manifold condition the flight deck and hold as separate zones (§5.9.2); in: engine/APU bleed, ram air, EPS.

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers drive two outflow valves (either sufficient) with pneumatic backup and independent mechanical relief; hold sized to low differential (preliminary) (§5.9.2); out: cabin altitude to AVI and OXY logic.

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove unacceptable ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect surfaces and inlets against ice
functions.subDef: Hot bleed air protects wing leading edges and engine cowls; six independently controlled electrically-heated stabiliser zones (§5.10.2); in: cross-bleed air, AC/DC power.

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove unacceptable ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect probes and detect icing conditions
functions.subDef: Probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and individually monitored; detection advisory with automatic or manual activation (§5.10.2); out: ice detection advisory to flight deck.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Four display units and two HUDs driven by three display processors on dual networks; three air-data inertial reference units plus an independent standby instrument sharing nothing with the primaries (§5.11.2); out: displays to crew, commands to autopilot/autothrottle.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where required and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU (AND logic degrading to single-loop), overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays, and nine-station hold smoke detection (§5.12.2); out: warnings to crew alerting.

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where required and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair discharged by crew via fire handles; dedicated APU bottle discharged automatically when unattended (§5.12.2); note hold has detection but no suppression (recorded assumption).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for depressurisation, smoke and fume events and the following diversion (SDD §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feed four quick-donning demand masks with smoke goggles; sized for four occupants for the diversion time; no passenger oxygen (§5.13.2); in: cabin-altitude signal from ECS.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust increase on one or more engines
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust rise produces unexpected acceleration and, if on one side, a yawing/rolling moment; at the 28 m outboard moment arm an asymmetric increase demands rudder to hold heading. Most demanding near the ground (approach/landing, takeoff) where speed/path management is time-critical.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded increase, counter with rudder/pitch, and attempt to isolate the affected engine via fuel shut-off / fire handle; workload elevated in a low-altitude phase.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only, exposed to the handling upset.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the function definition does not establish whether an increase is symmetric or asymmetric, the achievable magnitude, or whether FADEC overspeed/overthrust protection bounds it (SDD 5.1.6 states FADEC protects against overspeed/overtemperature but not against a commanded-thrust error). Aircraft effect (loss of control vs recoverable) is not derivable from the provided function alone.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust reduction on one or more engines
fha.effAc: Loss of available thrust below commanded; if asymmetric, a yawing moment at the 28 m outboard arm requiring rudder; if on takeoff/climb it degrades climb performance and path control at low energy. The aircraft is designed to continue after loss of one engine at/after V1, but an uncommanded reduction may not present as a clean single-engine failure.
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise thrust deficit, counter asymmetry, and manage the affected engine; performance/path management workload in a low-altitude phase.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the function definition does not fix whether the reduction is symmetric or asymmetric, the number of engines affected, or the magnitude, and whether it remains within the one-engine-inoperative design case. Aircraft-level outcome is not derivable without that.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Thrust not tracking commanded lever position
fha.effAc: Delivered thrust does not follow the thrust-lever command, so crew inputs do not produce the expected thrust response; degrades precise energy/path management. If it manifests differently across engines it introduces asymmetry demanding rudder.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the command/response mismatch, cross-check thrust indications against lever position, and manage thrust manually; recognition workload elevated.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the function definition does not establish the direction, magnitude, or number of engines affected by the mistrack, nor whether it is detectable via the engine parameter indication (SDD 5.1.4 lists engine parameter data to the display system). Aircraft effect ranges too widely to classify without that.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Gradual thrust erosion, not annunciated (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Slow reduction in delivered thrust below the commanded value that accumulates without annunciation; if asymmetric it produces a slow-developing yaw and drag/fuel penalty. Because it is below annunciation threshold the crew continue normally and take no corrective action, so the deficit is discovered late.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties with no action taken; recognition occurs only at a later cue (e.g. performance shortfall, imbalance).
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the unaware case depends on the magnitude the erosion can reach before another cue triggers, and whether it is symmetric or asymmetric — none of which is fixed by the function definition. Whether the late-discovered deficit threatens continued safe flight cannot be derived from the provided input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust, symmetric
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust available with no net asymmetry (no yawing moment), degrading climb gradient and performance margins; most demanding at takeoff/climb where climb capability is limiting for the 392,000 kg MTOW freighter. No directional-control demand since symmetric.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage a performance shortfall — adjust profile, assess climb/obstacle capability, plan diversion if margins inadequate; no asymmetry to counter.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the function definition does not quantify how much thrust is lost (fraction of total) or over how many engines, so the effect on climb/performance margin — and hence whether continued safe flight and landing is assured — cannot be derived. Symmetry is stated, magnitude is not.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust — asymmetric thrust producing a yawing moment
fha.effAc: Yawing/rolling moment; asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control; rudder authority must offset it; increased crew workload and degraded climb/cruise performance.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect asymmetry via engine parameters and yaw, apply rudder and retrim, and manage thrust; continue to a suitable aerodrome.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: outboard asymmetric thrust is the directional-control sizing case; a single asymmetry is controllable with rudder and crew action per the design intent to continue to a suitable aerodrome, indicating significantly increased workload rather than loss of control — confirm against directional-control sizing and rudder-authority margin. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust — slow asymmetric thrust drift below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effCrew: Crew assumed unaware; continue normal duties and take no corrective action for the drift.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD establishes the drift is below the detection threshold and unannunciated, but does not support stating the aircraft-level end effect of an undetected slow asymmetry (e.g. accumulated fuel/CG imbalance or eventual controllability margin). Needs the developed effect before a severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all engines)
fha.effAc: Total loss of thrust from all four engines; aircraft cannot sustain flight; forced descent/landing outside available performance.
fha.effCrew: Crew face a total loss-of-thrust emergency; RAT deploys automatically on loss of all AC generation to supply system C and the emergency generator, preserving essential control; attempt a forced landing.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: total loss of all propulsive thrust removes the ability to sustain flight and precludes continued safe flight and landing — maps to Catastrophic (Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh objective). Confirm; the target drives the propulsion-independence and IFSD-rate substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded in-flight thrust-reverser deployment
fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight on an inboard engine produces large asymmetric drag and yaw plus loss of forward thrust; potential loss of control depending on phase and airspeed.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to sudden yaw/asymmetry; deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical translating-sleeve lock, so this condition requires defeat of those interlocks.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: an uncommanded in-flight reverser deployment is a recognised potentially-catastrophic condition (asymmetric drag/yaw, possible loss of control), tending to Catastrophic in adverse phases — confirm against the reverser inhibit architecture (WOW + radio-altimeter + mechanical lock) which is the mitigation to be credited. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Thrust reverser fails to stow after selection
fha.effAc: Reverser remains deployed when stow is expected; residual reverse thrust/drag from an inboard engine on rollout or during a rejected-takeoff/go-around transition; asymmetry if only one inboard affected.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage residual reverse thrust and any asymmetry during deceleration; may need to reduce affected engine to idle and continue with wheel braking (predicted rollout ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m requirement).
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class from the provided material alone: the effect depends on whether the failed-to-stow reverser occurs on the ground (managed within braking margin) or during a go-around/RTO transition (thrust/asymmetry penalty), and the SDD does not resolve that operational context or the go-around case. Needs the developed effect per phase before a worst-case severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of reverse-thrust ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust deceleration on rollout; wheel braking remains the primary deceleration means with the design margin (1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout). Increased stopping distance, absorbed by braking margin on a normal surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply increased braking; higher workload on a degraded/short semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight, no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reverse thrust is supplementary and fitted to inboard engines only; wheel braking with stated stopping margin remains available, so partial loss is a slight increase in workload/stopping distance. CONFIRM against actual accountability of reverse thrust in the certified landing distance on a semi-prepared surface — if reverse credit is required to meet 1,800 m on a degraded surface, this rises to Major. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust producing a yawing moment on rollout
fha.effAc: Yawing moment during ground rollout from unequal inboard reverser deployment; directional deviation counteracted by nose-wheel steering and differential braking. Potential for lateral runway excursion if uncorrected on a narrow semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect yaw and apply steering/differential braking correction; increased workload during a high-tempo phase.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight, no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on the uncorrected yaw magnitude, available directional-control authority on the semi-prepared surface, and runway/strip width margin — none of which are quantified in the SDD. Cannot derive severity without the directional-control response and excursion outcome; leaving blank rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of reverse-thrust ground deceleration
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust contribution to ground deceleration; wheel braking remains the primary deceleration means with the stated margin (1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout). Increased stopping distance absorbed by braking margin on a normal surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on wheel braking and autobrake; increased attention to stopping distance, more so on a degraded/short semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight, no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity hinges on whether reverse-thrust credit is required to meet the 1,800 m landing distance on a semi-prepared surface. The SDD states braking margin is the basis of the flotation/braking design but does not state whether reverse thrust is accounted in certified landing distance. Cannot derive severity without that landing-distance accountability; leaving blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches other than as commanded; potential departure from intended flight path and possible exceedance of structural/aerodynamic envelope depending on magnitude and phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response, override or reconfigure to a degraded control law / mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion; high workload, especially at low altitude on approach or take-off.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight, no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous response of the primary pitch axis can drive an uncontrolled departure or envelope exceedance with limited crew reaction time at low altitude; proposed Catastrophic on the worst applicable phase. CONFIRM against the flight-control failure effects and the residual authority of the mechanical stabiliser-trim/lower-rudder reversion path — if the reversion path assuredly bounds the excursion, this may reduce to Hazardous. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches without command; departure from intended flight path and possible envelope exceedance depending on rate, magnitude and phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion and arrest it via inceptor input, degraded law, or mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion; high workload, worst at low altitude.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight, no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded motion of the primary pitch axis can produce an uncontrolled flight-path departure with limited recovery margin at low altitude; proposed Catastrophic on the worst applicable phase. CONFIRM against the detection means (envelope-protection/alerting), the recovery time available, and the bounding authority of the mechanical reversion path. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command (roll axis moves opposite or disproportionate to command)
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls in a direction or magnitude not matching the crew command; departure from intended flight path in roll. FBW voting on three dissimilar computers and dual actuation per surface (ailerons on HYD B and C) are the design defences against a single erroneous command path.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter it; envelope protection active in normal law. At low flight levels the time to arrest an erroneous roll is limited.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous roll response, if it defeats the crew's ability to maintain flight path, is a loss-of-control precursor; at the low flight levels this aircraft operates, unarrested roll leads to terrain impact. Proposed Catastrophic — confirm against the residual case after the three-computer vote and dual actuation are credited. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls with no crew input; hardover or drift in roll away from intended attitude. Dual actuation from HYD B and C and the three-computer vote are the defences; there is no mechanical reversion in roll (reversion is to stabiliser trim and lower rudder only).
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an uncommanded roll and counter it with no roll reversion path if all computers are lost. Low altitude limits recovery margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded roll with no mechanical reversion in the roll axis is a loss-of-control condition at low altitude. Proposed Catastrophic — confirm against the credited redundancy (dual actuation, three-computer vote) for the residual probability. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command (yaw axis moves opposite or disproportionate to command)
fha.effAc: Aircraft yaws in a direction or magnitude not matching the crew command. Split rudder in upper/lower segments on HYD A and B respectively; directional control is the sizing case for an outboard engine-out at V1 with max blade payload, so erroneous yaw directly threatens the engine-out controllability margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter erroneous yaw; lower segment has mechanical reversion. Erroneous yaw during the engine-out V1 case leaves minimal margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous yaw response undermines the directional-control margin the rudder is explicitly sized for (outboard engine-out at V1, max payload); at that condition loss of directional control is Catastrophic. Proposed Catastrophic — confirm against the split-segment/lower-segment reversion defence. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft yaws with no crew input; rudder hardover or drift. Split rudder on independent supplies (A upper, B lower) with lower-segment mechanical reversion; a single-segment hardover is bounded by the split arrangement, a full uncommanded yaw is a directional-control loss.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter uncommanded yaw; lower-segment mechanical reversion available. Low-altitude, high-payload operation limits recovery margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded yaw is a loss-of-directional-control precursor; the split-segment design bounds a single-segment case but a full uncommanded yaw at low altitude is Catastrophic. Proposed Catastrophic — confirm whether the split-segment arrangement caps this condition at a lower class for a single-segment hardover. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch motion below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches slowly with no command and below the threshold at which the condition is annunciated; unarrested, the divergence progresses toward an out-of-trim or unusual attitude. Whether crew scan, autopilot behaviour, or monitoring arrests it before an unrecoverable attitude is not established by the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Assumed unaware (below detection threshold) and continuing normal duties; no action taken regarding this condition until effects become perceptible.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided material: the effect depends on how far the slow uncommanded pitch progresses before it is detected and arrested, and the SDD does not state a detection threshold, an autopilot disconnect/monitoring behaviour, or a time-to-unrecoverable for pitch. Missing: monitoring/annunciation threshold for slow pitch drift and the recoverability margin once detected. Do not classify until these are supplied — a slow undetected divergence could range from Major to Catastrophic depending on them.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll motion about the roll axis, below the crew/system detection threshold, with the crew unaware and taking no corrective action
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops an uncorrected roll excursion that grows undetected; may progress to a bank/attitude and, with the 72.6 t single-blade payload, a lateral load state from which timely recovery is not assured
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties, receive no annunciation, and take no action against the drift until it manifests as a gross attitude change
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point to a potentially severe outcome (undetected roll excursion with a large unitised payload), but the provided function definition and SDD do not quantify the excursion rate versus detection threshold, the envelope-protection floor, or the attitude reached before it becomes annunciated — cannot ground the boundary between Hazardous and Catastrophic. Left empty per abstention; engineer to classify once the drift/detection dynamics are defined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded yaw motion about the yaw axis, below the crew/system detection threshold, with the crew unaware and taking no corrective action
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops an uncorrected yaw/sideslip that grows undetected; sideslip on the outsized high-wing configuration couples into roll and increases structural/directional load, potentially reaching a state from which recovery is not assured
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties, receive no annunciation, and take no action against the drift until it manifests as a gross heading/sideslip change
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects indicate a potentially severe undetected excursion, but the SDD does not define the yaw drift rate versus detection threshold, the sideslip limit, or the coupling with the split-rudder authority sizing case — cannot ground whether the reached state is Hazardous or Catastrophic. Left empty per abstention; engineer to classify once the drift/detection and sideslip limits are defined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous steady surface bias about any axis (pitch, roll or yaw), not annunciated, with the crew unaware and taking no corrective action
fha.effAc: A standing erroneous surface offset degrades trimmed flight, biases the attitude response about the affected axis and erodes control-authority margin; with the blade payload and engine-out directional sizing case a persistent bias reduces the reserve the aircraft was sized to hold
fha.effCrew: Crew fly the aircraft with a hidden offset, may mis-trim or mis-compensate, and receive no discrete indicating the erroneous bias
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The definition establishes an undetected erroneous bias but does not bound its magnitude, the axis affected, or how much control-authority margin it consumes relative to the engine-out/blade-loaded sizing case — the aircraft effect could range from a workload increase to loss of adequate authority. Insufficient grounding to select a single class; left empty per abstention for engineer disposition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded attitude control about the three axes, within the manoeuvre/controllability limits the aircraft is sized to, with the crew aware via annunciated degraded control law
fha.effAc: Reduced control authority or degraded response about one or more axes, but the aircraft remains controllable within its sized envelope; margins to the engine-out/blade-loaded directional sizing case are reduced
fha.effCrew: Degraded control law is annunciated; crew fly with increased workload and any applicable degraded-law procedure, remaining within controllable limits
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Attitude control remains within the limits the aircraft is sized to, the degradation is annunciated (§5.3.6 degraded laws annunciated), and the effect is a significant reduction in safety margin / increase in crew workload rather than loss of control — consistent with Major (↔ Remote, 1e-5/fh) under AC 25.1309-1B. Confirm the phase set and that no phase drives the effect higher. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded attitude control about the three axes with the impairment exceeding the manoeuvre/controllability limits the aircraft is sized to (outside MAC limits), crew aware
fha.effAc: Control authority or response degraded beyond the limits the aircraft was sized to hold; the aircraft may be unable to maintain the trajectory required, especially against the outboard-engine-out at 28 m arm with maximum blade payload sizing case, with recovery not assured
fha.effCrew: Crew face a controllability situation beyond the design margin; workload and required precision may exceed what can be sustained, particularly in the critical take-off/landing phases
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects describe control degraded beyond the sized controllability limits, which points to the severe end (Hazardous or Catastrophic). But the SDD does not quantify how far outside the MAC/controllability boundary this condition sits, nor whether adequate residual control remains in the driving phase, so the split between Hazardous (1e-7/fh) and Catastrophic (1e-9/fh) cannot be grounded. Left empty per abstention; engineer to classify against the directional-control sizing case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority; elevators driven from HYD A and C with the trimmable stabiliser retained; aircraft controllable at increased crew workload and possibly reduced envelope.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain pitch attitude and trim; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects show controllability retained (elevators on two hydraulic systems plus stabiliser) but with significant reduction in safety margin and increased crew workload — consistent with Hazardous. Engineer to confirm against §25.1309 and the FCS sizing case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced roll control authority; ailerons driven from HYD B and C with multi-function spoilers available; aircraft controllable at increased crew workload and possibly reduced roll rate.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain lateral control and coordinate turns; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects show roll control retained (ailerons on two hydraulic systems plus spoilers) with reduced margin and increased workload — consistent with Hazardous. Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced yaw control authority; split rudder with upper segment on HYD A and lower on HYD B, and mechanical reversion available to the lower segment; directional control sizing case is an outboard engine failure at V1 with max blade payload, so reduced yaw authority erodes the margin against the sizing asymmetric-thrust case.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to hold heading and counter any asymmetric thrust; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects show yaw control retained (split rudder segments plus mechanical reversion) but directly reducing margin against the outboard-engine-out directional sizing case — significant reduction in safety margin, consistent with Hazardous. Engineer to confirm; if a single rudder-supply loss is shown to leave insufficient authority in the sizing case, severity may rise. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of attitude control about three axes
fha.effAc: Loss of the ability to control aircraft attitude about all three axes; only mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment remains, which is a survivable-but-degraded means and does not restore three-axis attitude control; loss of control of the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to maintain controlled flight; only degraded mechanical reversion available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aboard beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects describe loss of aircraft attitude control with no full-authority recovery path (mechanical reversion is degraded and partial only) — outcome is loss of the aircraft, consistent with Catastrophic. Engineer to confirm against §25.1309. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: High-lift position not matching selection
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces (Fowler flaps in four sections, full-span slats) at a position other than commanded; asymmetry brakes at each section limit but do not eliminate a differential-deployment rolling moment; a position/selection mismatch alters lift, drag and stall margin and, if asymmetric, introduces an uncommanded rolling moment during the low-speed take-off, approach and landing phases.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to recognise the mismatch and manage configuration; performance recomputation required; asymmetry/jam discretes annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects show a configuration/asymmetry mismatch during low-speed phases that degrades stall margin and can introduce a rolling moment bounded by asymmetry brakes — significant reduction in safety margin and increased workload, consistent with Hazardous. Engineer to confirm; the actual severity depends on the maximum credible asymmetry the brakes permit, which is not quantified in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement (asymmetric or symmetric) not matching the commanded configuration
fha.effAc: Uncommanded change in high-lift position alters lift, drag and pitching moment; if asymmetric, produces a rolling/yawing moment. During take-off, approach or landing the change in configuration and any asymmetry degrades control margins in a phase with low energy and little altitude for recovery.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded movement, diagnose configuration state and counter any asymmetry while managing a critical low-altitude phase; workload increases significantly.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded (uncommanded high-lift change with possible asymmetry in take-off/approach/landing), but the SDD does not state the achievable authority/asymmetry-brake limits or the controllability outcome, so the boundary between Hazardous and Catastrophic cannot be derived from the provided material. Leaving severity blank for engineering determination against the FCS controllability case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of high-lift extension/retraction — configuration attainable only partially or at reduced rate
fha.effAc: Reduced or partial high-lift results in higher take-off/approach/landing speeds and increased required runway; on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout the margin is eroded, and configuration for the achievable field length may not be met.
fha.effCrew: Crew select alternate configuration/performance, recompute speeds and distances and may divert; workload elevated but a managed procedure exists.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is grounded (partial high-lift raising speeds/distance against a stated narrow landing margin), but the SDD does not state how much high-lift remains available for a single-PDU or single-section loss, so the resulting speed/distance penalty and its severity cannot be derived. Severity left blank pending FCS/performance data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment — left/right sections at different positions
fha.effAc: Left/right high-lift asymmetry produces a rolling and yawing moment requiring lateral/directional control input to trim; in take-off, approach or landing this degrades control margin at low speed and low altitude. Asymmetry brakes at each section limit the divergence.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the asymmetry, hold corrective input and manage the approach/landing with reduced margins; workload elevated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded (asymmetric high-lift rolling/yawing moment at low speed), and the SDD confirms asymmetry brakes exist, but the limited asymmetry those brakes permit and the resulting controllability outcome are not stated, so the Hazardous-vs-Catastrophic boundary cannot be derived. Severity left blank pending asymmetry-brake and controllability data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration capability — high-lift unavailable in any position
fha.effAc: With no high-lift, take-off and landing must be flown clean, raising stall, approach and touchdown speeds substantially and increasing required field length; on an 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m nominal rollout the landing margin is eroded and a suitable field may not exist within range.
fha.effCrew: Crew fly a no-flap/no-slat approach and landing at elevated speeds, recompute performance and select a suitable diversion field; workload significantly increased in the landing phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is grounded (clean take-off/landing at elevated speeds against a narrow stated landing margin on a semi-prepared strip), but the SDD does not quantify the clean-configuration landing distance or whether a compliant field is available, so whether the outcome is Hazardous or Catastrophic cannot be derived from the provided material. Severity left blank pending performance data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to achieve down-and-locked landing gear configuration prior to landing
fha.effAc: Gear not down-and-locked means the aircraft cannot be supported on its gear for landing; a landing in that state collapses the affected leg(s), leading to structural damage and loss of ground control on touchdown. A free-fall alternate extension exists as a backup means of achieving the configuration.
fha.effCrew: Crew attempt free-fall alternate extension and confirm downlock via dual proximity sensing; if unsuccessful they face an off-nominal landing with high workload and limited options.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is grounded (inability to achieve down-and-locked configuration for landing, with a free-fall alternate available), but the SDD does not state the outcome of landing with a leg not down-and-locked (e.g. occupant survivability, controllability on a partial-gear touchdown), so the severity cannot be derived from the provided material. Severity left blank pending the landing-outcome determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear/downlock status indication presented to the crew
fha.effAc: Displayed gear/downlock state does not match true state; crew may commit to landing on an unsafe configuration or reject a sound one, risking gear collapse or hard touchdown of a 392,000 kg aircraft on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew acts on false configuration information; workload and error potential increase; alternate-extension decision made on wrong premise.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single derived severity without the correct-indication defence: SDD states downlock is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit, so whether a single erroneous indication is annunciated/cross-checked (aware) or masks true state (unaware) drives the class. Needs the aware/unaware split and the true-state assumption before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous downlock (down-and-locked) indication presented despite a unit not locked
fha.effAc: Crew believes gear down-and-locked when a unit is not; on touchdown the unlocked unit may collapse, causing loss of ground support at max landing weight (318,000 kg) on a semi-prepared surface, with structural damage and possible departure from the surface.
fha.effCrew: No warning of the true unsafe state; crew continues normal landing and takes no corrective action (alternate extension not commanded); high potential for injury.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: a false down-and-locked indication defeats both the annunciation and the free-fall-alternate defence (crew unaware, takes no action), so an unlocked bogie collapses on touchdown of a 318 t aircraft on a semi-prepared strip — plausibly loss of the aircraft. PROPOSED Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh) for engineer confirmation; the two independent downlock circuits are the argument that must make this Extremely Improbable. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support capability (reduced gear/bogie support)
fha.effAc: One or more bogies fail to carry full load; aircraft support degraded but not lost; increased footprint pressure on the remaining units and possible asymmetry, with risk of sinkage or bogie damage on a semi-prepared surface at up to 318,000 kg landing weight.
fha.effCrew: Crew manages degraded configuration; increased workload for directional and rollout control on the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a single class: 'partial loss' spans a wide degradation band (one bogie of six vs. a full gear leg) and the SDD gives no residual-support or load-redistribution capability for a partial gear loss. Need the specific degradation extent and remaining support margin on the semi-prepared surface before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of footprint flotation on a semi-prepared surface (support geometry intact, bearing capacity exceeded)
fha.effAc: Tyre/footprint pressure exceeds what the semi-prepared surface bears; gear sinks or ruts; aircraft may bog down, veer, or suffer gear/structural damage during rollout or taxi at up to 318,000 kg.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses effective ground control/mobility; increased workload; potential inability to complete rollout or clear the surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: flotation was sized to the semi-prepared surface via twenty tyres derived from a tactical airlifter, but the SDD gives no surface bearing-strength assumption or flotation-loss aircraft effect (excursion vs. controlled stop). The design bearing basis and the loss-case effect are the missing inputs.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support of the aircraft (aircraft cannot be supported on its gear)
fha.effAc: Aircraft not supported on landing/rollout; fuselage/structure contacts the surface at up to 318,000 kg landing weight on a semi-prepared strip; severe structural damage and loss of control on the ground.
fha.effCrew: No means to arrest or control the aircraft on the ground; high potential for fatal injury to the flight crew.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: total loss of ground support at touchdown means the aircraft is not carried on its gear and the airframe strikes the surface at 318 t on a semi-prepared strip — loss of the aircraft and plausibly the crew. PROPOSED Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh) for engineer confirmation; the six-bogie/free-fall-alternate architecture is the argument that must make total loss Extremely Improbable. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel-braking deceleration
fha.effAc: No wheel-braking deceleration available on ground; deceleration relies on reverse thrust (inboard engines only) and aerodynamic drag; on a semi-prepared strip with landing distance requirement 1,800 m against ~1,080 m predicted rollout the residual means may be insufficient, risking overrun beyond the prepared surface. During RTO the loss of braking removes the primary stopping means at the most demanding energy case.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply reverse thrust and available alternate/accumulator means; workload high; directional and stopping management demanding at RTO/landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point to a potential overrun that could be Hazardous or Catastrophic, but the outcome depends on the stopping margin achievable with reverse thrust plus aerodynamic drag alone on a semi-prepared surface, and on whether accumulator/alternate braking is truly absent in this condition — neither is quantified in the SDD. Severity left empty pending that margin analysis rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced wheel-braking deceleration capability
fha.effAc: Reduced braking effectiveness (e.g. single hydraulic supply or accumulator-supported braking) lengthens rollout; on a semi-prepared strip the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout is the basis on which braking degradation is assessed, so a partial loss erodes but may not exhaust that margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew supplement with reverse thrust; increased stopping distance managed within displayed margin; workload increased.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Major: reduced deceleration lengthens rollout and reduces safety margin on a semi-prepared surface but is designed to remain within the requirement given the stated margin and available reverse thrust — a significant reduction in safety margin with increased crew workload, not by itself life-threatening. Confirm against the actual degraded-braking distance. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking on rollout
fha.effAc: Unequal left/right braking generates a yawing moment during the ground roll, tending to pull the aircraft off the runway centreline; on a semi-prepared strip of limited width a directional excursion risks departure from the prepared surface. Anti-skid operates per wheel pair and nose-wheel steering is available to counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter the yaw with steering and differential technique; workload high during high-energy rollout; timely correction required to avoid excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects indicate a potential directional excursion whose severity depends on the magnitude of the braking asymmetry, the available steering authority to counter it, and the prepared surface width — none of which the SDD quantifies. Severity left empty pending that controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded braking with no pedal input
fha.effAc: Braking applied without crew command decelerates the aircraft unexpectedly; if uncommanded and asymmetric it also yaws the aircraft; during the take-off roll it degrades acceleration and take-off performance, and on rollout/taxi it produces unexpected deceleration and possible directional deviation with associated tyre/brake energy and gear loading effects.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter unexpected deceleration/yaw and may need to isolate the affected brake; workload elevated, recognition time critical during take-off roll.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on whether the uncommanded braking is symmetric or asymmetric, its magnitude, the flight phase (a take-off-roll case is more demanding than taxi), and the crew's means to isolate it — the SDD does not characterise the malfunction magnitude or isolation, so classification is not grounded and is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced deceleration undetected until landing rollout
fha.effAc: A latent reduction in braking capability is not revealed until braking is applied on the landing rollout, when the crew have no opportunity to plan for the shortfall; on a semi-prepared strip with a limited margin between the 1,800 m requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout, an undetected shortfall consumes stopping distance that cannot be recovered, raising overrun risk beyond the aware partial-loss case.
fha.effCrew: Crew are unaware pre-landing and take no accommodating action; on discovery they apply maximum available reverse thrust and remaining braking with little time to react.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Because the shortfall is unannunciated until the critical phase, the outcome trends more severe than the aware partial loss and could reach an overrun, but the severity still depends on the magnitude of the undetected reduction and the residual stopping means — unquantified in the SDD. Left empty pending the degraded-braking distance analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground directional control by nose-wheel steering
fha.effAc: No steering authority on the ground; directional control during take-off roll and landing rollout must be maintained by rudder and differential braking (SDD lists dual-supply braking and anti-skid). On a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, ability to hold centreline and stop within available surface with rudder/differential braking only is not established in the provided material.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain directional control by rudder and asymmetric braking; crew commands steering from tillers and rudder pedals per SDD.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without the aircraft-level effect at the boundary: whether rudder plus differential braking alone maintains directional control and centreline on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface, and the runway-excursion outcome if they do not. SDD gives the landing-distance margin but not steering-loss controllability. Missing: directional-control-with-steering-lost analysis and excursion consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced ground steering authority
fha.effAc: Degraded but available steering; larger turn radius / reduced steering rate, partially compensated by rudder and differential braking. Effect on ability to hold centreline within available surface not quantified in the provided material.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to manoeuvre and hold centreline with degraded steering.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the degree of authority reduction and its effect on centreline-keeping / excursion margin on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface is not derivable from the function definition. Missing: quantified authority reduction and its directional-control consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous steering response to crew command
fha.effAc: Steering deflects other than as commanded; potential for uncommanded directional deviation, at speed on take-off roll or landing rollout, toward a runway/taxiway excursion on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip. Countered by crew rudder/braking and, per SDD, a mechanical disconnect for towing (not established as an in-motion mitigation).
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous deflection and counter with rudder and differential braking; detection time and available authority to recover at speed not established.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: recoverability of an erroneous steering deflection at ground-roll speed, and the excursion outcome if not recovered, is not derivable from the provided function/architecture material. Missing: steering-malfunction controllability and excursion consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded steering deflection with no crew command
fha.effAc: Nose-wheel deflects with no command (steering hardover / runaway); at take-off or landing-rollout speed this drives a rapid directional divergence toward a runway excursion on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip. Recovery depends on crew countering with rudder and differential braking within available surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded deflection and arrest the divergence with rudder and asymmetric braking; time-critical, higher workload than a commanded case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft response to an uncommanded steering hardover at speed, its recoverability, and the excursion outcome are not derivable from the provided material. Missing: hardover controllability analysis and excursion consequence on the semi-prepared surface.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced steering authority undetected until ground manoeuvre
fha.effAc: Latent reduction in steering authority not annunciated; first manifests when steering is demanded during a ground manoeuvre or landing rollout, when the crew has no prior awareness and cannot pre-plan. Effect on centreline-keeping / excursion margin on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface not quantified.
fha.effCrew: Crew is unaware of the degradation and takes no compensating action until steering under-responds during a manoeuvre; detection is late and reaction time compressed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the consequence of discovering reduced authority only at the point of demand — and whether rudder/braking recovers the resulting deviation on the semi-prepared surface — is not derivable from the provided material. Missing: late-detection controllability and excursion consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Nose door drives in the wrong direction to command
fha.effAc: Door moves opposite to selection during a ground door operation; potential mechanical damage to visor structure or hold interface. Door cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.6), so no in-flight aircraft effect.
fha.effCrew: Ground crew detects wrong-direction motion from ground handling panel indication and halts the operation.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is confined to a ground door operation with detection at the handling panel; the SDD gives no basis to state a safety-relevant aircraft effect beyond potential structural damage, whose magnitude and structural consequence are not established here. Requires structural/operational assessment to classify — left empty rather than defaulting to No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose door drive activation
fha.effAc: Door drive runs without a command during a ground operation. Door cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.6) and a pressure interlock prevents unlock with residual differential above 0.1 psi (§5.7.2), so an uncommanded unlock in flight is inhibited.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not authored in the current SF-008 FCIM and is drafted per this turn's request. The SDD interlock (§5.7.2) and ground-only operation (§5.7.6) bound the in-flight case, but the ground-collision/structural consequence and the credibility of an uncommanded drive against the interlock are not established here — cannot classify without further analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced nose door drive capability requiring backup
fha.effAc: Primary hydraulic (system A) door drive degraded; door operated on the electric backup drive (§5.7.2). No in-flight effect — door not operated in flight (§5.7.6).
fha.effCrew: Ground crew selects/continues on backup drive; operation slower but completed.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Backup drive exists (§5.7.2) so the ground function is retained; the only effect implied is a slower turnaround, which the SDD frames as a dispatch/turnaround consideration, not an aircraft safety effect. No aircraft-level effect is stated in the definition to classify — left empty rather than assuming No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door open/close capability
fha.effAc: Neither primary nor backup door drive available; the hold cannot be opened or closed for loading/unloading. Door not operated in flight (§5.7.6), so no in-flight aircraft effect; impact is a dispatch/turnaround inability at a strip with no line maintenance (§1.1).
fha.effCrew: Ground crew cannot load or unload the payload; aircraft cannot be dispatched with the intended payload state.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Total loss prevents a ground loading operation but has no stated in-flight aircraft effect. Whether this is No Safety Effect at aircraft level or a door-left-open configuration hazard depends on the door's failed state (open vs closed-and-locked) at the time of loss, which the definition does not fix. Cannot ground a classification — left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous lock-engaged indication presented to the flight deck with the door unsecured
fha.effAc: Flight deck and take-off configuration monitor indicate the nose door locked when it is not secured. The door forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed (§5.7.1); with latches/pins not engaged, in-flight failure of the boundary can lead to visor departure, rapid depressurisation of the hold, and loss of the forward structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Crew dispatch with false lock-engaged indication and no annunciation; on boundary/structural failure the crew face a rapid depressurisation and potential loss of control with little warning.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants exposed, but structural failure threatens the aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Erroneous lock-engaged indication with the door unsecured defeats the dual dissimilar sensing intended to prevent an undetected unsecured door (§5.7.2/§5.7.5); the door is a single-load-path structural and pressure-boundary element (§5.7.1/§5.7.3). Undetected in-flight loss of that element (visor departure / structural load-path loss) is consistent with a Catastrophic outcome per §25.1309, mapping to Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh). Confirm the failed-door structural/aeroelastic consequence with structural and special-condition analysis (nose door special condition anticipated, §1.3). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded unlock actuation of nose door locking
fha.effAc: Nose visor lock pins driven out of engagement without command; visor is a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage structural load-path element when closed (SDD §5.7.1). On the ground with the pressure interlock and ground-only operation intact, loss of locking is contained to a ground event. If unlock actuation can occur in flight against the pressure interlock, loss of the pressure boundary and forward structural load path follows.
fha.effCrew: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and included in the take-off configuration check (SDD §5.7.6); crew becomes aware via loss-of-lock indication and inhibits despatch / initiates the configuration remedy.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD §1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Aware case: crew alerted by lock-status indication and take-off configuration monitor; despatch/take-off inhibited. Severity leans entirely on the pressure interlock and ground-only operation preventing an in-flight unlock; that barrier is not yet validated, so worst credible in-flight outcome is retained as Hazardous pending confirmation of the interlock's integrity. Confirm severity. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of nose door lock integrity with both sensing paths misreading engaged
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical linkage/visual indicator) misread the pins as engaged while lock integrity is lost (SDD §5.7.2). Visor is a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage structural load-path element when closed (SDD §5.7.1). Undetected loss of locking with the visor a single load path and no in-flight remedy places the pressure boundary and forward structural load path at risk of release.
fha.effCrew: Both sensing paths indicate lock engaged, so the crew is unaware, receives no alert, and continues normal duties taking no action (unaware condition per ARP4761A).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD §1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Unaware condition: dual dissimilar sensing defeated, no crew alert, no action. If the visor can release in flight — a single structural load path and pressure boundary with no redundancy in the door structure (SDD §5.7.3) — outcome is loss of the aircraft. Severity hinges on whether an in-flight release is physically credible given ground-only operation; confirm both the release mechanism and the severity. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial latch/pin engagement of nose door locking
fha.effAc: A subset of the twelve latches / eight pins engage (SDD §5.7.2), leaving the visor pressure-boundary and forward structural load-path element only partially secured. Reduced lock margin against flight and pressure loads on a single-load-path structure.
fha.effCrew: Lock status displayed on the flight deck and included in the take-off configuration check (SDD §5.7.6); the dual dissimilar sensing paths (SDD §5.7.2) provide the means of detection, so the crew is alerted to incomplete engagement and inhibits despatch/take-off.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD §1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the SDD does not state the structural/pressure margin retained under partial engagement (how many of twelve latches / eight pins must engage), nor whether the sensing paths reliably distinguish partial from full engagement. Without the residual capability the effect on the aircraft cannot be bounded to derive a class. Engineer to supply partial-engagement structural margin and sensing resolution.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door locking
fha.effAc: No latch or pin engagement of the nose visor. Visor is a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage structural load-path element when closed (SDD §5.7.1) with no redundancy in the door structure and treated as a single load path (SDD §5.7.3). Complete loss of locking leaves the visor unsecured against flight and pressure loads.
fha.effCrew: Lock status displayed on the flight deck at all times and included in the take-off configuration check (SDD §5.7.6); dual dissimilar sensing (SDD §5.7.2) alerts the crew to unsecured status and despatch/take-off is inhibited.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD §1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Aware case detected on the ground/pre-take-off inhibits despatch. Severity is set by the worst credible outcome: an unsecured single-load-path pressure-boundary visor released in flight loses the aircraft. Ground-only operation and the pressure interlock are the barriers; the aware-and-inhibited path may reduce the effective severity, but the underlying condition's worst case is Catastrophic. Confirm severity and whether the aware/inhibited path is creditable at aircraft level. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint tension indication
fha.effAc: Tension monitoring loop presents an incorrect strap-tension state for the single 72.6 t blade payload (SDD §5.8.1/§5.8.2). Erroneous indication (either masking a genuine restraint loss or falsely indicating a loss) misleads the crew about the actual restraint state; a genuine but masked loss risks blade movement against flight and ground load cases, with a large single mass shifting the load path and CG.
fha.effCrew: In flight the crew has indication only and there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint (SDD §5.8.6); an erroneous indication either provokes an unnecessary response or conceals a genuine restraint loss, and no corrective in-flight action is available to restore restraint.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD §1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Erroneous indication of a 72.6 t single-blade restraint state is misleading with no in-flight remedy; a masked genuine loss could allow blade movement affecting CG/structure. Severity is not fully bounded because the SDD does not state the aircraft response to a restraint loss in flight (whether blade movement is controllable/survivable), so Hazardous is a proposal pending the restraint-loss aircraft effect. Confirm severity. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of payload restraint at a station within a tension-loop monitoring coverage gap (no annunciation to the crew)
fha.effAc: Restraint is lost on part of a single unitised blade of up to 72.6 t occupying the full hold length without crew awareness; potential for uncommanded longitudinal blade movement and centre-of-gravity/load-path excursion whose magnitude is not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action as the condition is not annunciated; no in-flight adjustment of restraint is available.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction (undetected partial restraint loss on a 72.6 t blade) is credible but the SDD does not quantify the coverage-gap extent or the resulting load shift, so a defensible aircraft-level effect magnitude cannot be established. Severity left empty pending tension-loop coverage-gap analysis and blade load-shift analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced restraint at one saddle station, with the lost strap load carried by neighbouring stations
fha.effAc: Load path from a single lost strap is carried by neighbouring stations by design; blade restraint remains effective with reduced margin; no uncommanded blade movement.
fha.effCrew: Loss of tension on the strap is annunciated in flight; crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment; condition monitored.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Minor: SDD states load paths are sized such that loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so the aircraft-level effect is a reduced restraint margin that is annunciated — a slight reduction in safety margin, no loss of function. Confirm against the restraint load-path substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint of the single unitised blade over the full hold length
fha.effAc: Complete loss of restraint of a single blade of up to 72.6 t occupying the full 108 m hold length; uncommanded longitudinal blade movement and gross centre-of-gravity excursion, with potential for loss of aircraft control and/or fuselage structural overload.
fha.effCrew: Restraint loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a condition requiring immediate attention; crew has indication only with no in-flight means of re-restraint.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Catastrophic: total loss of restraint of a 72.6 t unitised blade over the full hold length is a credible large CG-excursion / structural-overload / loss-of-control path. Confirm against blade load-shift, CG-excursion and fuselage structural analyses. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous indication of adequate restraint tension while actual restraint is degraded or lost (monitor masks a real restraint condition)
fha.effAc: A real degradation or loss of restraint is masked, denying the crew awareness and any procedural response; the aircraft-level effect is that of the underlying unannunciated restraint condition, whose magnitude is not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew are misled into believing restraint is adequate and take no action; no in-flight adjustment of restraint is available.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect of this erroneous monitor is bounded by the underlying restraint loss it masks; the SDD does not quantify the extent of restraint that could be lost while indicated adequate, so a defensible severity cannot be derived. Left empty pending the restraint load-shift analysis and tension-loop failure-coverage analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous indication of lost restraint tension while restraint is in fact intact (false/nuisance restraint annunciation)
fha.effAc: Restraint remains fully intact; the aircraft is not affected mechanically; effect is a false annunciation only, potentially prompting a precautionary crew response such as a diversion.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive a spurious restraint annunciation; crew has indication only and no in-flight adjustment, so the achievable response is precautionary (e.g. reduced manoeuvring or diversion); slight increase in workload.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Minor: restraint is actually intact, so no direct aircraft effect; the consequence is a nuisance annunciation and a possible precautionary diversion — a slight increase in crew workload. Confirm against the false-annunciation crew-workload and diversion-policy assessment. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of restraint tension monitoring (crew aware of the monitoring loss)
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Landing
fha.effAc: No loss of restraint capability itself; the aircraft loses all in-flight indication of strap tension state, so any subsequent restraint degradation would be undetected. Detectable at dispatch as loss of the take-off configuration restraint status input.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware monitoring is lost; can address at origin as a dispatch decision (no line maintenance at the strip, outbound/return considered together per SDD). No in-flight adjustment of restraint is possible regardless.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loss of monitoring alone causes no immediate aircraft effect and is crew-detectable; but the aircraft-level severity depends on whether dispatch/continued flight without restraint monitoring is acceptable given the single 72.6 t blade — the SDD does not state the consequence of an undetected restraint failure occurring while monitoring is absent. Needs SF-010 restraint assessment + loads/CG input before classifying. Left empty rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected complete loss of restraint tension monitoring (crew unaware)
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Landing
fha.effAc: Crew continue normally believing monitoring is functional; the aircraft has no coverage of strap tension, so any restraint degradation of the 72.6 t blade proceeds with no annunciation. Potential for undetected blade shift, CG excursion and load-path overstress if a strap or station fails in flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no action; no cue that the "two adjacent stations" restraint warning can no longer be raised. No in-flight restraint adjustment exists in any case.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The controlling consequence is a restraint failure occurring WHILE monitoring is silently lost — its aircraft effect (blade shift, CG/controllability, structural load path) is not quantified anywhere in the SDD. Cannot derive severity without the SF-010 restraint failure effects and loads/structural input. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of tension monitoring coverage (crew aware — a segment of the loop is annunciated as lost)
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Landing
fha.effAc: No loss of restraint capability; monitoring remains over the unaffected stations but a segment of the single instrumented loop no longer reports. Reduced insight into a portion of the hold length.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware coverage is degraded to a known extent; can weigh continued flight / dispatch with reduced coverage. No in-flight restraint adjustment available.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect of losing coverage over one segment depends on whether an undetected restraint failure in that segment is consequential — that consequence is not quantified in the SDD (single instrumented loop, coverage recorded as an open item). Cannot classify without SF-010/loads input. Left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of monitoring coverage on a segment (crew unaware a portion of the loop no longer reports)
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Landing
fha.effAc: Crew continue normally believing full-length monitoring is active; restraint degradation within the silently uncovered segment would not be annunciated. Localised undetected restraint failure possible on the single 72.6 t blade over that portion of the hold.
