fha.effCrew: Crew take no action regarding the coverage gap; the "two adjacent stations" restraint warning may fail to be raised for the affected segment. No in-flight restraint adjustment exists.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Same unquantified dependency as the other undetected conditions: the aircraft effect turns on the consequence of an undetected restraint failure within the uncovered segment, which the SDD does not characterise. Needs SF-010 effects + loads/structural input. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous indication of adequate restraint tension (monitoring reports the blade adequately restrained when it is not)
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Landing
fha.effAc: Crew and take-off configuration monitor receive positive (adequate) restraint status while true restraint is degraded or lost. The 72.6 t single blade may be inadequately restrained with no cue in any phase; take-off could be initiated on false restraint status, and in-flight restraint failure would proceed with false reassurance. Potential blade shift, CG excursion and load-path overstress.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no corrective action — indication actively contradicts the true state; the erroneous "adequate" status defeats both the strap warning and the take-off configuration check. No in-flight restraint adjustment available.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This misleading-indication condition is the most safety-significant of the set because it corrupts the take-off configuration decision and defeats the restraint warning, but the aircraft-level severity is driven by the effect of the erroneously-permitted inadequate restraint (blade shift / CG / structure), which the SDD does not quantify. Severity cannot be derived from the monitoring function alone — requires SF-010 restraint effects and loads/structural substantiation. Left empty rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous conditioned-air temperature delivery
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Which zone receives the erroneous temperature (occupied flight deck vs unoccupied hold) drives the crew effect, and the ECS description gives no thermal tolerance or exposure to quantify a flight-deck effect. Aircraft effect not stated. Cannot classify — needs the crew-zone thermal effect and its duration.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded loss of flow to a zone
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; loss of hold flow has no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which zone loses flow. Loss of flight-deck ventilation could affect the crew, but the description gives no time-to-effect or thermal/CO2 consequence to derive from; loss of hold flow affects no occupant. Aircraft effect not stated. Cannot classify — needs the flight-deck ventilation-loss consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous conditioned-air delivery developing slowly
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect for the hold zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Slow undetected erroneous delivery with the crew taking no action — but the ECS description states no thermal tolerance, exposure limit, or downstream effect for the flight deck, so no aircraft/crew effect can be derived. Cannot classify — needs the crew-zone consequence of a slow undetected drift and the delay to detection.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of air conditioning capacity
fha.effAc: Single-pack operation is permitted; conditioning continues at a reduced hold conditioning schedule.
fha.effCrew: Crew selects pack configuration; the residual pack covers essential conditioning per the reduced schedule.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; reduced hold conditioning schedule has no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced schedule, which points to a benign residual, but it does not state the crew-zone effect of degraded conditioning nor bound the reduced schedule, so an aircraft-level effect cannot be derived and a class cannot be established. Cannot classify — needs the flight-deck effect under reduced capacity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of distribution to one conditioning zone
fha.effPax: If the hold zone loses distribution: hold is unoccupied, no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which of the two zones loses distribution. Flight-deck distribution loss could affect the crew but the description gives no consequence or time-to-effect to derive from; hold distribution loss affects no occupant. Aircraft effect not stated. Cannot classify — needs the flight-deck distribution-loss consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of air conditioning / distribution capacity (crew unaware, no annunciation)
fha.effAc: Reduced conditioning to flight deck and hold; conditioned-air capacity degraded below scheduled without indication. Fuselage pressure control per SF-013 unaffected.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew continue normal duties and take no action. Flight-deck thermal/air-quality environment degrades gradually.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without the flight-deck cabin-altitude / conditioning schedule and the degree/rate of degradation the 'partial' covers, and whether undetected loss of conditioning can progress to a crew-incapacitation-relevant environment. SDD gives redundancy (two packs, single-pack permitted with reduced schedule) but no environmental limit that would drive severity. Missing: flight-deck conditioning limits and the failure magnitude.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution
fha.effAc: Total loss of conditioned-air supply to flight deck and hold. Pressure control (SF-013) is a separate function; loss of conditioning does not itself vent the fuselage. Independent mechanical relief remains.
fha.effCrew: Loss of flight-deck conditioning; crew environment degrades. Crew oxygen available for smoke/fume/breathing but does not restore ambient conditioning. Diversion/descent likely required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: the SDD does not state the flight-deck cabin-altitude schedule or the environmental limits that determine whether total loss of conditioning threatens crew capability within the diversion time. Effect on aircraft is bounded (pressure control is independent) but crew-environment consequence is unquantified. Missing: flight-deck conditioning limits and time-to-effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous overpressurisation command (fuselage differential driven above intended)
fha.effAc: Outflow valves commanded toward closed erroneously, driving differential above schedule on a low-differential hold structure and a nose-visor pressure boundary. Independent positive-pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.
fha.effCrew: Overpressure annunciated via differential/cabin-altitude indication; crew select manual mode / alternate configuration. Positive relief limits the excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Structural consequence of overpressure depends on the (preliminary, not frozen) hold differential and relief-valve set point margins, which the SDD does not quantify. With independent positive-pressure relief present the excursion is bounded, but whether the bounded excursion is Major or worse cannot be derived from the SDD. Missing: hold differential design value and relief set-point margin.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous underpressurisation / uncommanded depressurisation (fuselage differential driven below intended)
fha.effAc: Outflow valve(s) commanded open erroneously or differential otherwise driven down; cabin altitude rises. Two controllers, two outflow valves and a pneumatic backup mode are available; negative-pressure relief protects independently.
fha.effCrew: Rising cabin altitude annunciated; crew don quick-donning oxygen masks and initiate descent/diversion per procedure. Crew oxygen sized for four occupants for the diversion time at max operating altitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: the depressurisation rate, the flight-deck cabin-altitude schedule, and time-of-useful-consciousness margin against the crew-oxygen diversion sizing are not quantified in the SDD. Crew oxygen and multiple control paths are protective, but whether an uncommanded depressurisation is Major or Hazardous depends on rate and altitude data not provided. Missing: max operating altitude time-to-effect, depressurisation rate, cabin-altitude schedule.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow erroneous differential pressure drift (crew unaware, no annunciation)
fha.effAc: Differential drifts slowly away from schedule below detection/annunciation threshold; cabin altitude departs intended value gradually with control system believing state is nominal.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew continue normal duties and take no action. Slow cabin-altitude rise can reach a physiologically significant level before independent relief or a downstream alert intervenes.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: whether undetected slow drift reaches crew-incapacitation-relevant cabin altitude before any independent cue depends on the flight-deck cabin-altitude schedule, the drift rate, and the cabin-altitude warning threshold — none of which the SDD quantifies. This is the credible-worst-case of the SF-013 malfunctions because it defeats the crew-awareness protection, but the numbers to set the class are absent. Missing: cabin-altitude warning threshold and drift-rate bound.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fuselage differential pressure control
fha.effAc: Fuselage cannot maintain any commanded differential; hold and flight-deck pressurisation lost. Structure protected independently by mechanical relief valves per SDD. Aircraft must descend to a safe altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware via cabin altitude/differential indication and alerting; assumed to don oxygen masks (quick-donning, sized for the diversion at max operating altitude) and initiate emergency descent to a breathable altitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight — no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: outcome depends on whether the emergency-descent-plus-crew-oxygen response reliably prevents crew incapacitation at FL260 over the diversion time. The SDD states oxygen is sized 'for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve' but does not give the descent profile or time-of-useful-consciousness margin to classify the effect. Needs analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of differential pressure control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced control authority over fuselage differential; differential held with degraded margin or at reduced schedule. Single-pack/degraded operation is a permitted reduced hold-conditioning schedule per SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via differential/cabin-altitude indication and alerting; assumed to manage altitude and, if margin eroded, descend. Increased monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight — no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity without knowing how much differential authority is retained and the resulting cabin-altitude excursion. 'Partial' is unquantified in the source; the effect on crew (oxygen need vs none) depends on the residual schedule, which the SDD does not state. Needs the degraded-schedule definition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic control with manual mode available
fha.effAc: Automatic pressurisation control lost; differential maintained through the manual mode and/or pneumatic backup driving one outflow valve directly on cabin pressure. Independent mechanical relief remains.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via loss-of-auto annunciation; assumed to select manual/monitor the pneumatic backup and manage the schedule manually. Increased workload but pressurisation retained.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight — no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Minor (↔ Probable): pressurisation function is preserved by the manual mode and the pneumatic backup ('either valve being sufficient'), so no cabin-altitude excursion is asserted; effect is a workload increase and loss of automation, a slight reduction in safety margin. Confirm the manual/backup mode reliably holds the schedule without excursion. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow loss of differential pressure control
fha.effAc: Slow, unannunciated drift of fuselage differential; cabin altitude rises gradually toward the ambient/relief condition without crew action, because the loss is below detection threshold.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware — assumed to continue normal duties and take NO action. Insidious exposure to rising cabin altitude with no oxygen donning until (if ever) a hard limit or symptom is reached.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight — no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the unaware case turns on the drift rate versus the altitude at which crew incapacitation begins at FL260, and whether any independent hard-limit alert exists below the primary threshold. The SDD gives neither the drift bound nor a backstop cabin-altitude warning, so the crew-incapacitation outcome cannot be established. Needs analysis of detection coverage and time-to-symptom.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous absence of surface/inlet ice protection with system indicated active
fha.effAc: Ice protection not actually provided on protected surfaces/inlets while indication shows the system active; ice accretes on wing leading edges and/or engine inlet cowls in the icing envelope, degrading aerodynamic performance and inlet flow with no annunciation prompting corrective action.
fha.effCrew: Crew misled by 'active' indication — assumed to continue in icing conditions taking no protective action, since the erroneous status defeats the cue to select manual protection or exit icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight — no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the aircraft effect depends on the accretion rate and the handling/performance degradation on this configuration in the certification icing envelope, and on whether an independent ice detector still cues the crew despite the false 'active' status. The SDD states detection is advisory with two same-type detectors but does not quantify the accretion consequence, so the effect cannot be classified. Needs icing performance analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded surface/inlet ice protection heating when not required, crew aware (system annunciates protection status per SDD §5.10.6)
fha.effAc: Bleed and/or electrical power drawn for protection not needed; pack conditioning capacity reduced when wing/cowl bleed anti-ice is active (SDD §5.10.4 states a bleed demand that reduces pack capacity). No adverse aerodynamic or structural effect from protection running.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe unwanted protection active on status display and can deselect (manual selection available at any time per §5.10.6); increased monitoring, no immediate handling task.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect is a resource/capacity penalty (reduced pack capacity) and a nuisance the crew can annunciate-and-deselect, with no aircraft handling or structural consequence grounded in the SDD; consistent with a slight reduction in functional capability / slight increase in crew workload. Confirm against the icing/bleed-demand quantification, which the SDD marks preliminary. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of surface/inlet ice protection with no zone annunciation, crew unaware (assume crew continue duties normally and take no action)
fha.effAc: Protection absent on affected surface/inlet with no health indication; in the icing envelope, ice accretes on an unprotected surface with the crew unaware. Aircraft effect (handling/performance/inlet degradation) depends on which surface and the accretion severity, which the SDD does not quantify.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware — no annunciation, no crew action assumed; the loss is masked because the failure defeats the zone annunciation the crew would otherwise rely on.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states detection is monitored per-zone but does not define the icing envelope of the certification basis or the aerodynamic/performance/inlet consequence of ice on an unprotected surface, and gives no crew detection path once annunciation is lost. Aircraft effect cannot be stated at a level that derives a severity. Need the icing envelope and the handling/performance degradation from ice on each protected surface.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of surface/inlet ice protection, crew aware (a lost zone is annunciated per SDD §5.10.3)
fha.effAc: Protection retained on part of the surfaces/inlets, lost on part; in the icing envelope ice may accrete on the unprotected portion. Magnitude of aircraft handling/performance effect depends on which portion is lost and accretion severity, not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the lost coverage (annunciated), may exit icing conditions or amend the plan; performance penalty of anti-ice in use is applied automatically to displayed performance (§5.10.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: although the loss is annunciated, deriving the severity requires the aerodynamic/performance consequence of ice on the unprotected portion within the certification icing envelope, which the SDD does not state. Do not assume the benign end. Need the icing envelope and the handling/performance degradation per lost coverage.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one independently supplied heated stabiliser zone (one of six), crew aware (lost zone annunciated per SDD §5.10.3)
fha.effAc: One of six independently controlled/supplied stabiliser leading-edge heat zones lost; five zones retain protection. Loss confined to a single stabiliser segment with the remaining zones and independent supplies unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the specific lost zone (annunciated); can avoid or exit icing conditions; displayed performance already reflects anti-ice use.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is grounded (single of six independently supplied zones lost, annunciated) but severity still depends on the aerodynamic consequence of ice on one stabiliser segment within the icing envelope, which the SDD does not quantify. A slight-degradation classification is plausible but cannot be derived without that data — left empty rather than assume the benign end. Need per-zone accretion/handling effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of bleed-supplied surface protection (wing leading edges / engine inlet cowls), crew unaware (assume crew continue duties normally and take no action)
fha.effAc: Hot-bleed protection to wing leading edges and/or engine inlet cowls absent with the crew unaware; in the icing envelope ice accretes on unprotected wing/inlet surfaces. Aircraft effect (lift/drag/handling on the wing, inlet ice ingestion to engines) depends on accretion severity and the icing envelope, not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware — no crew action assumed; the loss is not attributed to a zone annunciation in the SDD for the bleed-fed surfaces, so degradation may progress without cue.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: severity of undetected wing/inlet ice within the certification icing envelope (handling degradation, possible engine inlet ice ingestion) is not quantified in the SDD, and no bleed-surface health annunciation is described that would bound crew awareness. Aircraft effect cannot be stated precisely enough to derive a class; do not reach for the benign end. Need the icing envelope, the wing/inlet accretion consequence, and any bleed-protection monitoring.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of surface and inlet ice protection
fha.effAc: No protection of wing/tail leading edges, engine inlet cowls or probes in the icing envelope; ice accretion degrades lift, increases drag and can disturb engine inlet flow and probe sensing.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect and exit icing; degraded handling and potentially unreliable air data if probe heat is lost with the bleed/electrical protection.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Total loss of ice protection in the certification icing envelope threatens continued safe flight through accretion-driven performance/handling loss; Hazardous proposed as a floor. Confirm against the icing performance case — the SDD does not quantify the accretion effect, so a Catastrophic determination cannot be excluded without that data. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous icing detection when no icing present
fha.effAc: Nuisance activation of ice protection when not required; applies the wing anti-ice performance penalty and draws bleed reducing pack capacity with no icing present.
fha.effCrew: Nuisance advisory; crew may deselect; minor workload and a performance penalty applied automatically.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Detection is advisory and the penalty is a performance/economic effect the crew can manage by deselection; slight workload increase supports Minor. Confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous absence of icing indication in icing conditions
fha.effAc: Genuine icing conditions not indicated; automatic activation not triggered, so ice may accrete before the crew manually selects protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew not alerted to a real icing threat; manual selection remains available at any time but relies on independent crew recognition of icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: the SDD states detection is advisory with manual selection available at any time, but does not state whether the crew would independently recognise icing and act, nor the accretion consequence before manual activation. Severity turns on that crew-recognition credit and the icing performance case, neither of which the SDD provides.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to detect icing conditions
fha.effAc: Both detectors fail to detect actual icing with no annunciation; automatic activation not triggered and no indication that detection has failed.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware detection has failed and unaware of the icing; continue normal duties, taking no protective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: the unaware case severity depends on the accretion consequence in the icing envelope and whether the crew would recognise icing by other means, neither of which the SDD quantifies. The two ice detectors are of the same type (recorded common-cause item), but the resulting aircraft effect is not stated, so no severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of icing detection with probe protection retained
fha.effAc: Automatic icing detection lost; probe, static, windshield and detector heating retained, so air data protection is preserved; surface/inlet protection can still be selected manually.
fha.effCrew: Loss of the automatic detection advisory; crew retains manual selection of ice protection at any time; modest increase in monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Detection is advisory and manual selection remains available with probe protection retained, so air data integrity is preserved; the effect is a modest workload increase supporting Minor. Confirm against the crew-procedure assumption for manual selection. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of probe and static-port heating
fha.effAc: Reduced heating margin on some probes/ports in icing conditions; residual heated probes and the independent standby air-data path retain a usable air-data source, but exposure to probe icing is increased on the affected channels.
fha.effCrew: Annunciation of a lost heater zone; crew monitor and cross-check air-data, may exit icing conditions per procedure. Procedure not stated in the SDD.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; nominal crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect cannot be bounded from the SDD: whether partial heater loss degrades a used air-data source or is fully covered by remaining heated probes plus the independent standby path is not stated, nor is the crew procedure. Cannot derive severity without the number of independent air-data channels affected and the icing-exposure consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of a single probe heater
fha.effAc: A single probe heater fails without annunciation; in icing conditions that probe may ice over, corrupting or losing its air-data parameter. Whether the corrupted parameter is voted out by the remaining independent sources or propagates to displays cannot be determined from the SDD.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of the heater loss; crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding it. First cue would be an air-data disagreement if the probe subsequently ices.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; nominal crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected case: aircraft effect depends on whether a single iced probe is masked by voting across the three air-data reference units and the independent standby, or produces misleading air-data. The SDD states individual monitoring of heaters but the voting/coverage on loss of one heated source is not given, so the effect and hence severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe protection and icing detection
fha.effAc: In icing conditions all heated probes/ports and both ice detectors are unprotected/inoperative; multiple air-data channels can ice simultaneously, risking loss or corruption of primary airspeed/altitude information, and the crew is not alerted to icing onset.
fha.effCrew: Loss of automatic icing detection removes the cue to activate protection or exit; crew must recognise icing and degraded/erroneous air-data unaided and revert to standby air-data. Procedure and reversion outcome not stated in the SDD.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; nominal crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect could range to loss of primary air-data with no icing warning, but the SDD does not state whether the independent standby air-data path is separately heated/protected or whether it too is lost, nor the resulting flight-path consequence. Without the common-mode extent across air-data sources the worst-case aircraft effect cannot be bounded, so severity is left blank rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous display of flight information detectable by cross-comparison
fha.effAc: One display source presents erroneous flight information that disagrees with the independent standby instrument and the remaining primary sources; the discrepancy is detectable by cross-comparison, so the erroneous source can be identified and rejected. A transient before detection may cause a brief flight-path excursion, not characterised in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect the disagreement, identify the faulty source and revert to the standby instrument that shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; nominal crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Because the error is detectable by cross-comparison against an independent standby (SDD §5.11: standby shares no supply, sensor or processing), the crew can identify and reject it, bounding the effect at a significant increase in workload with no undetected loss of flight information — consistent with Major. Contingent on the pre-detection transient being benign; engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous display of navigation information detectable by cross-comparison
fha.effAc: Erroneous navigation information is presented but disagrees with the independent/redundant navigation sources (dual radio and satellite navigation, dual flight management), so the discrepancy is detectable by cross-comparison and the faulty source can be identified. Effect on flight path before detection not characterised in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to cross-check navigation sources, identify the erroneous source and revert to the valid one; heightened vigilance during the affected phase.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; nominal crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Detectability by cross-comparison against redundant navigation means (dual radio/satellite navigation, dual flight management per SDD §5.11.2) lets the crew identify and reject the erroneous source, bounding the effect at a significant workload increase without undetected misleading navigation — Major. Contingent on redundant nav sources being independent enough for reliable cross-comparison and on a benign pre-detection transient; engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight information consistent across sources
fha.effAc: Erroneous attitude/airspeed/altitude presented identically across primary and standby sources; consistency defeats cross-comparison and the independent standby, so the crew has no cue that the information is false. Aircraft flown to erroneous references risks loss of control or controlled flight into terrain.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the error and continue normal duties, acting on false references with no alerting or disagree indication.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected, source-consistent erroneous flight information with no crew cue and the standby defeated can lead directly to loss of control or CFIT — a condition preventing continued safe flight and landing. Proposed Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1x10^-9/fh) for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous navigation information consistent across sources
fha.effAc: Erroneous position/track/navigation guidance presented identically across sources with no disagree cue; aircraft flown to a false navigation solution. In IMC in low flight levels this risks controlled flight into terrain, particularly on approach to a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continue navigating on false guidance with no alerting.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is CFIT-tending, but severity depends on the degree of independent situational awareness retained (raw attitude/altitude, terrain awareness, ATC/radar) and the exposure phase, none of which the SDD resolves. The function definition 'Present flight and navigation information' does not by itself fix whether erroneous navigation alone is Catastrophic or Hazardous. Left empty pending engineer judgement on retained awareness and worst-case phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary display information with standby instrument available
fha.effAc: Primary flight/navigation display lost; independent standby attitude, airspeed and altitude remain available (shares no supply, sensor or processing with primaries). Aircraft controllable on standby references at increased crew workload; navigation capability degraded.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via loss of primary displays and revert to the standby instrument; increased workload and reduced situational information, particularly demanding in IMC/approach.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of primary display with an independent standby retained is a significant reduction in capability and a significant increase in crew workload, without loss of continued safe flight and landing. Proposed Major (↔ Remote, 1x10^-5/fh) for engineer confirmation; confirm whether IMC/approach workload could elevate to Hazardous. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of navigation information with attitude/airspeed/altitude retained
fha.effAc: Navigation information lost while attitude, airspeed and altitude remain available; aircraft controllable but position/track guidance degraded. In IMC in low flight levels, ability to navigate and approach a semi-prepared strip is reduced, mitigated by ATC/radar and dual navigation redundancy.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of loss of navigation information; increased workload and reliance on external services and remaining sensors.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of navigation with full basic flight information retained is a significant capability reduction and workload increase without threatening continued safe flight and landing. Proposed Major (↔ Remote, 1x10^-5/fh) for engineer confirmation; confirm dual FMC/nav redundancy and available fallback (ATC/radar) support this rather than Minor. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information display
fha.effAc: All flight and navigation information display lost, including the independent standby instrument; crew has no displayed reference for attitude, airspeed, altitude or navigation. In IMC this precludes safe control of the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of total loss of displayed information; no reversionary display remains, extreme workload with no reliable reference in IMC.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all displayed flight and navigation information, standby included, leaves no reference for control in IMC and would prevent continued safe flight and landing. Proposed Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1x10^-9/fh) for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or nuisance alerting with correct annunciation of the discrepancy
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft state; a spurious or nuisance alert is presented but the alerting system correctly annunciates the discrepancy, so the crew can identify it as erroneous.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload and distraction resolving a false alert; correct annunciation of the discrepancy bounds the potential for an inappropriate crew response.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are a nuisance/workload increment with the discrepancy correctly annunciated, bounding crew misresponse; a slight increase in workload consistent with Minor. Confirm against the specific alerts subject to nuisance and their crew-response implications. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to annunciate a genuine system condition
fha.effAc: Aircraft effect depends on which underlying system condition is not annunciated; ranges from negligible (a minor advisory) to safety-significant (e.g. a fire, engine or configuration condition) where the crew is deprived of the cue to act.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action regarding the unannunciated condition, since the failure is undetected; a genuine condition progresses unmitigated.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the alerting function definition alone: the aircraft effect is set by WHICH genuine system condition is not annunciated, and that criticality allocation is not stated in the provided material. Needs the alerting-criticality mapping (which annunciations are safety-critical) to derive severity for the worst-case lost alert.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected mis-prioritisation or suppression of a genuine alert
fha.effAc: Aircraft effect depends on the criticality of the alert mis-prioritised or suppressed; a high-priority genuine alert buried or suppressed deprives the crew of a timely cue, while a low-priority mis-order has negligible effect.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on a distorted alert picture; a genuine higher-priority condition may be masked by, or reordered behind, a lower-priority one, undetected, delaying or preventing the correct response.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the alerting function definition alone: severity is driven by WHICH alert is suppressed or mis-prioritised and the time-criticality of the associated procedure, which the provided material does not fix. Needs the alert prioritisation/criticality allocation to derive the worst-case severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew alerting with one processing channel retained
fha.effAc: Alerting continues on the retained processing channel of the two independent channels; alerting capability continues, potentially at reduced coverage or with reduced redundancy, but the crew alert function remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain an alerting means through the surviving channel; loss of the redundant channel is annunciated and increases exposure to a subsequent channel failure but does not by itself deprive the crew of alerts.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With one of two independent processing channels retained the alerting function continues; the effect is a loss of redundancy / possible slight workload increase. Proposed Minor pending confirmation that the retained channel provides full alert coverage and that any coverage reduction is annunciated. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting
fha.effAc: Both independent processing channels lost; the aircraft has no consolidated means of annunciating what has failed and what to do about it. Subsequent system failures across all monitored systems (fire, engine, configuration, hydraulic, electrical) would occur without crew alerting.
fha.effCrew: Crew are deprived of the consolidated alert list and associated procedures; failures must be detected by other cues (direct indications, aircraft behaviour), significantly increasing workload and the potential for an undetected or mishandled system failure, particularly time-critical ones.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loss of the whole alerting function is safety-significant but the aircraft-level severity depends on the assumed independent-cue coverage for the most time-critical monitored conditions (e.g. fire, engine) when alerting is unavailable. That coverage is not stated in the provided material; classify once the worst-case monitored condition without its alert is bounded.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious fire or overheat warning with no fire present
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Aircraft airworthy; no actual fire. Warning may drive an unnecessary engine/APU shutdown and fuel isolation via the fire handle, reducing available thrust/redundancy.
fha.effCrew: Crew perform fire drill for a non-existent fire: workload and distraction, potential unnecessary shutdown and diversion; can cross-check against absence of corroborating indications.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight (crew-only freighter); hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Major: nuisance warning drives crew fire drill and possible unnecessary engine shutdown/diversion with attendant workload, but aircraft remains controllable and crew can cross-check; confirm against §25.1309. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected fire or overheat below detection threshold or in an uncovered location
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: An actual fire/overheat is not annunciated; crew take no extinguishing action; fire may propagate in an engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct run, gear bay or hold (hold has detection but no suppression).
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties unaware; no fire drill initiated; first awareness may be secondary effects (structural/system damage), by which time response options are reduced.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous: an undetected fire denies the crew the means to respond; severity of an escalation to Catastrophic depends on an outside-monitored-zone or unsuppressed-hold fire propagation case the function definition does not establish — confirm with a fire-coincidence/zonal analysis. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in one monitored zone with detection retained elsewhere
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Fire/overheat in the affected zone is not detected; detection in all other monitored zones remains. A fire in the unmonitored zone would propagate unannunciated; other zones retain protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain detection and response capability for all other zones; loss of the affected zone's detection may be latent unless annunciated.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Major: loss of one protection layer that is latent and zone-limited; escalation depends on an undetected fire in that specific zone, which the function definition does not resolve — confirm and consider dispatch/latency. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded single-loop detection following loss of one loop
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection continues on the surviving loop with degraded single-loop logic; AND warning logic reduced to single-loop, increasing susceptibility to a missed or spurious warning in that zone. Detection function retained.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain fire detection and response; degraded loop annunciated; increased reliance on the single remaining loop until repair.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Major: detection retained on single loop with reduced redundancy and integrity; consequence of a subsequent second-loop failure or a missed detection is not established at function level — confirm against §25.1309 and latency. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No fire or overheat annunciation from any monitored zone (engine nacelles, APU, bleed duct runs, gear bays, hold). A fire in any protected zone would go undetected and unaddressed; extinguishing is a crew action that would not be initiated.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no means to detect fire/overheat; first awareness only via secondary effects; unable to initiate the correct fire drill in time.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous: total loss of the detection function denies fire response across all zones; classification as Catastrophic depends on the coincident occurrence of an actual fire (notably the unsuppressed hold), which the AFHA function level does not model — confirm with a coincident-fire/zonal analysis. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguisher discharge into a nacelle
fha.effAc: Fire-extinguishing agent discharged into a nacelle with no fire present; the affected engine pair's extinguishing reserve for that side is consumed. Effect on the running engine of agent ingestion/discharge is not established by the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive discharge status indication; workload to assess and manage the affected engine.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive aircraft effect: the SDD does not state whether an inadvertent discharge degrades or shuts down the running engine, nor whether it defeats subsequent genuine-fire protection for the pair (cross-plumbing consumed). Effect on continued flight is ungrounded — severity left blank pending the engine/agent-interaction and reserve-availability data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing capability for one engine pair with the other retained
fha.effAc: No means to extinguish a fire in either nacelle of one engine pair; a fire in that pair could not be controlled by the fire-protection system, though the opposite pair retains full protection. Fire detection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the extinguishing-system failure; increased workload and reliance on shutdown/isolation to manage a fire on the affected pair.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect only materialises if a nacelle fire also occurs in the affected pair; the outcome of an unextinguishable nacelle fire depends on fire-zone containment/burn-through timing and structural/systems consequences not stated in the SDD. Severity left blank pending the fire-zone burn-through and consequence analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of a single extinguisher charge with cross-plumbed reserve available
fha.effAc: One extinguisher charge unavailable; the cross-plumbed reserve bottle remains available to discharge into either nacelle of the pair, so a single shot of extinguishing capability is retained for that pair. Fire detection unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to reduced extinguishing reserve; no immediate operational change.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Full single-shot extinguishing capability is retained for the pair via cross-plumbing, so no loss of function under a single fire event; but whether the residual case supports a No-Safety-Effect or Minor classification depends on the dispatch/reserve policy and any second-fire assumption not stated in the SDD. Severity left blank pending that operational basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of engine and APU fire extinguishing capability
fha.effAc: No means to extinguish a fire in any engine nacelle or the APU compartment. A fire arising in any of these zones could not be controlled by the fire-protection system; crew are limited to shutdown, fuel isolation and fire-handle actions without agent discharge. Detection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to total loss of extinguishing; management of any subsequent engine/APU fire limited to isolation actions with no agent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An unextinguishable engine or APU fire is potentially severe, but the aircraft-level outcome (whether it threatens continued safe flight and landing) depends on fire-zone containment and burn-through timing, structural/systems vulnerability in the nacelle/APU zones, and the effectiveness of isolation alone — none stated in the SDD. Severity left blank pending the fire-zone consequence and burn-through analysis rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous low oxygen supply pressure to a mask
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft systems; the crew oxygen supply itself may be adequate while indication/regulation to one mask station erroneously presents or delivers low pressure.
fha.effCrew: A single crew mask station may deliver, or be indicated as delivering, insufficient oxygen. In a depressurisation, smoke or fume event the affected crew member's protection at that station is degraded; remaining mask stations and the crossover-fed reserve are unaffected. Crew workload increased to diagnose and reconfigure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level severity turns on whether the erroneous low pressure is a genuine delivery shortfall at one station versus indication only, and on the coincidence with a pressurisation/smoke event (a non-normal that itself sets the exposure). The SDD states four independent mask stations with independent regulators and a two-cylinder crossover but does not establish the crew-incapacitation consequence at a single degraded station. Severity left blank pending that operational/effect basis rather than assumed benign.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft controllability; the aircraft remains flyable. Consequence is realised only in a coincident cabin-altitude / smoke / fume event, where the crew have no protective breathing supply for the descent and diversion the aircraft would then need to perform.
fha.effCrew: With no oxygen available, a depressurisation, smoke or fume event leaves both crew subject to hypoxia or incapacitation; ability to conduct an emergency descent and diversion is lost. Loss is annunciated (low-pressure alerting, continuous cylinder pressure display).
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous: complete loss of crew oxygen does not by itself endanger the aircraft, but in a coincident depressurisation/smoke/fume event it produces crew incapacitation with no protective supply during the required descent/diversion — a large reduction in safety margins and crew capability. Not proposed Catastrophic because the loss is annunciated and the event requires a concurrent second condition. Confirm against the depressurisation profile and diversion-time margin, which are not in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one cylinder supply with crossover reserve at reduced duration
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft controllability. The remaining cylinder, via the crossover, still supplies the crew for the required duration but at reduced reserve, so tolerance to a prolonged diversion or a coincident event is reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain a breathing supply through the crossover; the single remaining cylinder is stated capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve. Loss of a cylinder is annunciated via continuous cylinder-pressure display and low-pressure alerting.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Minor: capability is retained through the crossover at reduced reserve, so the effect is a slight reduction in safety margins with the crew still protected for the required duration; the condition is annunciated. Confirm against the reserve-duration margin, which is not quantified in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen to one mask station with other stations retained
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft controllability; oxygen remains available at the other mask stations.
fha.effCrew: Oxygen is retained at the remaining mask stations; the affected crew member loses supply at that station. The SDD does not state whether that crew member can transfer to an unaffected station, so the resulting protection state for that individual cannot be established.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided function definition: the SDD states regulators are independent per mask but does not state whether an affected crew member can relocate to a spare/unaffected mask station, nor whether all donned stations are required simultaneously. Missing: the operational rule for mask-station reassignment and the minimum protected-crew requirement. Without these the aircraft/crew effect of losing one station cannot be grounded, so severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected insufficient oxygen delivery at a donned mask below crew perception
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft controllability. The hazard is to the crew: in a depressurisation/smoke/fume event the affected crew member receives insufficient oxygen while believing the mask is functioning.
fha.effCrew: An affected crew member, having donned the mask, receives insufficient oxygen below their perception and takes no corrective action; in a coincident cabin-altitude or fume event this leads to insidious hypoxia and possible incapacitation of that crew member without warning. The condition is by definition undetected, so no alerting is assumed.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous: undetected insufficient delivery to a donned mask can incapacitate the affected crew member without warning during a depressurisation/fume event — misleading in that the crew member believes they are protected — with no crew action taken. Not proposed Catastrophic because a second crew member and, where applicable, transfer to another station may remain available, and the effect requires a coincident event. Confirm against the depressurisation profile, monitoring coverage of delivered flow, and minimum protected-crew requirement, none of which are in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: Propulsion (PRP) is authored as an aircraft FUNCTION delivering thrust, while Fuel, Hydraulic, Electrical, Crew Oxygen and Wiring are excluded as RESOURCES.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 explicitly types PRP as Function and FUE/HYD/EPS/OXY/EWS as Resource; the modelling rule bars authoring resources as functions, so thrust behaviour is the function and its power/fuel/wiring supplies are consumed resources.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any of those resource systems must be represented as a function, an additional aircraft function and its decomposition would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide propulsive thrust; exclusion of Fuel/Hydraulic/Electrical/Oxygen/Wiring functions

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose-door structure and the hold-floor hard points are structure, not functions, and are excluded from the functional decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: The modelling rule bars structural integrity as a functional-FHA item; the SDD explicitly states the door is a single load path treated as structure and the hard points carry no redundancy.
assumptions.ifWrong: If structural load paths are to be modelled functionally, they would appear as functions feeding structural analysis / PRA instead.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at the nose; Restrain the cargo payload

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: Roll, pitch, yaw and high-lift are decomposed as independently-failable sub-functions of 'Control aircraft flight path' because each rides distinct surfaces and hydraulic supplies.
assumptions.rationale: §5.3.2 shows each axis on separate surfaces with distinct hydraulic-supply pairs and separate actuation, meeting the split-where-independent rule; high-lift shares a common torque shaft so is kept as one sub-function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the axes share a common failure means not visible here, they should be merged, changing the sub-function count and independence notes.
assumptions.usedFor: Control roll; Control pitch; Control yaw; Provide high-lift configuration

citations.quote: Every primary surface is driven by at least two actuators supplied from different hydraulic systems.

assumptions.text: Ground control is decomposed into gear support, deceleration and nose-wheel steering as separate sub-functions.
assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 shows retraction on system A, braking normally on system B, and steering as a distinct hydraulic means with mechanical disconnect — three independently-failable capabilities.
assumptions.ifWrong: If braking and steering share a dominant common supply that removes independence, they may merge, altering the decomposition.
assumptions.usedFor: Support and configure the landing gear; Decelerate on the ground; Provide nose-wheel steering

citations.quote: Retraction and extension is by hydraulic system A ... Braking is carbon multi-disc ... normally from system B

assumptions.ifWrong: If any of these is later deemed to accomplish an aircraft behaviour, an additional top function and sub-functions would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from the emitted add_function set.

assumptions.ifWrong: If the flight deck itself operated at a high cabin altitude, loss of oxygen would be immediately consequential in normal flight and the loss-of-function rows would classify more severely.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-TL, SF-020-M2, SF-020-PL severities

assumptions.ifWrong: If the reduced reserve is insufficient for the worst-case diversion time, SF-020-PL would rise from Minor toward Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-PL severity

citations.quote: either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve

assumptions.text: No passenger oxygen is required because the hold is unoccupied in flight and the crew complement is the only protected population.

assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all four rows

assumptions.ifWrong: If a single FCC output can drive the surface without being outvoted, the FCC branch becomes an OR (order-1 cut set), which is unacceptable for a Catastrophic condition and changes the tree structure.
