praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread release (§25.734 / AC 25.734-1) — 20 tyres on one twin-wheel nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies; debris size/energy/trajectory not grounded in provided material
praData.desc: Tyre burst or tread release in a main gear bay (710/720) or nose gear bay (730). In-zone contents per SDD §3: three bogies each, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses (710/720); nose unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect (730). Both main-gear-bay brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each bay in adjacent, separately clipped and shielded bundles sharing the bay (SDD §5.4.5/§5.6.5, recorded zonal item) — a single burst event in one bay is the credible common cause that could defeat the A/B brake-supply independence claim for that side. Debris trajectory/energy left empty: not grounded in the provided material.
praData.systems: LDG (wheel braking SF-006, ground support SF-005, nose-wheel steering SF-007); HYD systems A and B brake supply
praData.csfl: Tyre burst in a single main gear bay is a common physical cause across the nominally independent HYD A and HYD B brake supplies that share that bay (adjacent clipped bundles) — potential CSFL defeating the dual-hydraulic brake redundancy for that side. Reflect as a common-cause contributor in the wheel-braking fault trees rather than treating A and B brake supplies as independent in-bay.
praData.mitigation:
Separately clipped and shielded A/B brake-line bundles within each bay; steering and braking electrical harnesses routed on opposite sides of each bay (SDD §5.6.5); dual hydraulic brake supply (B normal, A alternate) plus accumulator reserve sized for six full brake applications with all three systems lost (SDD §5.4.3/§5.6.3). Effect claimed: to be shown ACCEPTABLE via the 1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout margin (SDD §1.1) — margin substantiation pending, provisional at drawing stage.
Proposed requirements: • The main gear bay installation shall protect brake hydraulic lines A and B against a common tyre-burst debris event such that a single burst does not defeat both brake supplies to that side (candidate — separation/shielding, to be substantiated).
• The zonal analysis shall reflect tyre burst in a single gear bay as a common-cause contributor in the wheel-braking fault tree, removing the in-bay A/B independence claim.
• The nose gear bay (730) installation shall protect the steering actuator against tyre-burst debris to preserve ground directional control (candidate).
aiFunctions: SF-006 Decelerate aircraft on the ground by wheel braking
SF-005 Support aircraft on the ground
SF-007 Provide ground directional control by nose-wheel steering
aiRequirements: The main gear bay installation shall protect brake hydraulic lines A and B against a common tyre-burst debris event such that a single burst does not defeat both brake supplies to that side (candidate — separation/shielding, to be substantiated).
The zonal analysis shall reflect tyre burst in a single gear bay as a common-cause contributor in the wheel-braking fault tree, removing the in-bay A/B independence claim.
The nose gear bay (730) installation shall protect the steering actuator against tyre-burst debris to preserve ground directional control (candidate).

praData.threat: Bird strike (§25.571(e)(1) / §25.631 / §33.76) — external forward-facing threat; bird mass/energy per applicable AC not grounded in provided material
praData.desc: Bird strike on forward-facing structure and inlets: flight deck / windshield (130), forward equipment bay region and probes/detectors on the forward fuselage (120, per SDD §5.10.2 two ice detectors and probes on opposite sides of the forward fuselage), nose visor structure (110), wing leading edges (510/520) and engine inlet cowls (610–640). In-zone contents per SDD §3: displays, inceptors, standby instrument, crew oxygen masks (130); FCC 1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks (120). Bird energy/mass and structural penetration threshold left empty: not grounded in the provided material (engine model definition not yet released, SDD §5.1.2).
praData.systems: PRP (thrust SF-001, ingestion); AVI (flight/nav display SF-016, air data via ADIRU and probes); IPS (probe heat and ice detection SF-015); FCS via air data input; NZD nose visor structure (110)
praData.csfl: Bird ingestion into one or more engines is a candidate common cause across the propulsion set only to the extent inlets are co-exposed; left/right engine pairs sit in separate zones with services not commingled outboard of the wing root (SDD §5.1.5), so a single strike is not credibly a four-engine common cause. Strike on forward-fuselage probes could be a common cause across air-data-derived functions where probes share the forward-fuselage location; the two ice detectors are identical in type on opposite sides (SDD §5.10.2, recorded commonality item) — reflect probe/detector co-exposure as a potential common-cause contributor in the flight-information and icing-detection fault trees.
praData.mitigation:
Left and right engine pairs in separate zones, services not commingled outboard of the wing root (SDD §5.1.5); single-engine-out continuation design case at/after V1 (SDD §5.1.3); triple-redundant dissimilar FCC and independent standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays (SDD §5.3.2/§5.11.2/§5.11.5); windshield structural/penetration substantiation to be shown per cert basis. Effect claimed: to be shown ACCEPTABLE (single-engine ingestion) / to be substantiated (windshield, probe co-exposure) — provisional at drawing stage.
Proposed requirements: • Forward-facing structure (nose visor 110, windshield 130, wing leading edges 510/520, engine inlets 610–640) shall withstand or survive the bird-strike threat of the cert basis without a Catastrophic effect (candidate — to be substantiated against §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76).
• Forward-fuselage probe and ice-detector installation shall provide sufficient physical separation that a single bird strike does not disable air-data sensing common to multiple flight-information functions (candidate — separation).
• The flight-information and icing-detection fault trees shall reflect forward-fuselage probe/detector co-exposure to bird strike as a common-cause contributor.
aiFunctions: SF-016 Present flight and navigation information
SF-015 Protect probes and detect icing conditions
aiRequirements: Forward-facing structure (nose visor 110, windshield 130, wing leading edges 510/520, engine inlets 610–640) shall withstand or survive the bird-strike threat of the cert basis without a Catastrophic effect (candidate — to be substantiated against §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76).

Forward-fuselage probe and ice-detector installation shall provide sufficient physical separation that a single bird strike does not disable air-data sensing common to multiple flight-information functions (candidate — separation).
The flight-information and icing-detection fault trees shall reflect forward-fuselage probe/detector co-exposure to bird strike as a common-cause contributor.

praData.threat: High-Intensity Radiated Fields (§25.1317, AC 20-158A) — external RF illumination coupling into aircraft electrical/electronic systems through apertures and cable pickup
praData.desc: HIRF illuminates the airframe; energy couples in through apertures (windshields/flight deck 130, nose visor 110 openings/seams) and onto cable runs, reaching flight-critical electronics in the equipment bays (120 FCC1/forward avionics, 300 FCC2/mid bay, 400 FCC3) and along the HV/LV/data routes that transit the wing (530/540) and hold (200/300/400). Failure conditions potentially caused by simultaneous RF upset of redundant electronics: FCS erroneous/uncommanded response FC-014, FC-015, FC-016, FC-017, FC-018, FC-019 and slow-drift undetected FC-020, FC-021, FC-022, FC-023; erroneous/undetected flight-and-navigation information (SF-016 FCIM Aware/Unaware); erroneous or failed crew alerting (SF-017 FCIM). Like lightning, HIRF is a common-cause threat that can defeat the three-dissimilar-FCC voting and the dual-network / independent-standby-instrument independence claims (SDD §5.3.2, §5.11.5) — CSFL across nominally independent FCS/AVI channels.
praData.csfl: HIRF upset common to all three FCCs and/or both network channels, or defeating the independent standby instrument on the DC essential bus, invalidates the FCS/AVI independence argument
praData.mitigation:
HIRF protection per §25.1317 / AC 20-158A: shielded/filtered cable interfaces, aperture treatment at windshields and the nose-visor seams, equipment-level susceptibility qualification of the FCCs, ADIRUs, display processors and FADECs; the SDD-declared HV/LV separation and opposite-side dual data-network routing (§5.11.5, §5.14.2). Protection LEVELS not yet substantiated in the SDD — acceptability is SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE pending §25.1317 test/analysis
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft shall demonstrate that the §25.1317 HIRF environment cannot simultaneously upset all three flight control computers, both data-network channels, or defeat the independent standby instrument.
• Flight-critical LRUs (FCCs, ADIRUs, display processing units, FADECs) shall be qualified to the §25.1317 HIRF equipment susceptibility levels.
• Aperture coupling at the flight-deck windshields and nose-visor seams shall be substantiated against the external HIRF environment.
aiRequirements: The aircraft shall demonstrate that the §25.1317 HIRF environment cannot simultaneously upset all three flight control computers, both data-network channels, or defeat the independent standby instrument.
Flight-critical LRUs (FCCs, ADIRUs, display processing units, FADECs) shall be qualified to the §25.1317 HIRF equipment susceptibility levels.
Aperture coupling at the flight-deck windshields and nose-visor seams shall be substantiated against the external HIRF environment.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structure and inlets (§25.571(e)(2))
praData.desc: High-energy hail impact on forward-facing surfaces: radome/nose visor structure (110), windshields (130), wing leading edges (510/520), empennage leading edges (800), and the four engine inlet cowls (nacelles 610-640). The two ice detectors and probes/static ports are mounted on the forward fuselage (per SDD, ice detectors on opposite sides of forward fuselage; FCC1/avionics in 120). Model as forward-hemisphere impactor; source is the icing/hail cloud ahead of the aircraft. Trajectory strikes windshield, radome, inlet lips and leading edges simultaneously (common external cause across otherwise-independent surfaces).
praData.systems: PRP (engine inlet ingestion, nacelles 610-640), AVI/IPS (probe and ice-detector damage feeding air data, zone 120/forward fuselage), FCS (leading-edge/high-lift surface damage), ECS/IPS (leading-edge bleed protection surfaces)
praData.csfl: Common external cause defeats the independence of the two ice detectors (identical type, opposite sides of forward fuselage) and can degrade multiple air-data sources at once; simultaneous multi-inlet ingestion can reduce thrust on more than one engine, eroding the engine-independence claim that underpins the one-engine-inoperative dispatch case.
praData.mitigation:
Substantiate hail impact resistance of windshields, radome/visor and leading edges to the §25.571(e)(2) threat; verify engine inlet and fan hail ingestion capability against the certified engine's declared hail standard; confirm probe/ice-detector siting and heating survive impact. Survivability claim: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE for structure and single-inlet ingestion subject to impact-resistance substantiation; MINIMISED for air-data by the independent standby instrument on the DC essential bus (shares no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries per SDD 5.11.3). Multi-inlet simultaneous thrust loss is retained as a condition to be studied.
Proposed requirements: • The forward-facing structure (radome/nose visor, windshields, wing and empennage leading edges) shall withstand the certification-basis hail impact threat without loss of the pressure boundary or the affected surface function.
• The two ice detectors and the air-data probes shall be sited and protected so that a single hail encounter cannot render all air-data sources erroneous without annunciation.
aiRequirements: The forward-facing structure (radome/nose visor, windshields, wing and empennage leading edges) shall withstand the certification-basis hail impact threat without loss of the pressure boundary or the affected surface function.
The two ice detectors and the air-data probes shall be sited and protected so that a single hail encounter cannot render all air-data sources erroneous without annunciation.

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding (§25.1419, AC 20-73A)
praData.desc: Two mechanisms modelled: (a) ice ACCRETION on unprotected or under-protected surfaces, inlets and probes where the ice protection system (IPS) fails or is defeated; (b) ice SHEDDING from wing/stabiliser leading edges and engine inlet cowls into the fan of nacelles 610-640, and shed-ice impact on aft structure/empennage (800). Wing leading edges and inlet cowls are bleed-protected through the shared cross-bleed manifold; the stabiliser leading edges are electrically heated in six zones; probes/detectors are electrically heated. Ice envelope is preliminary and must be refined to the type-design envelope.
praData.systems: IPS (SF-014 surface/inlet protection, SF-015 probe protection and detection), ECS (shares the cross-bleed manifold in zone 300), PRP (fan ingestion of shed ice, nacelles 610-640), FCS (accretion on high-lift/leading-edge surfaces affecting SF-004), AVI (probe icing feeding erroneous air data)
praData.csfl: The cross-bleed manifold in zone 300 is a shared bleed source for both engine-inlet and wing-leading-edge protection and for the ECS packs (SDD 5.10.2/5.9.2): a manifold or bleed-supply fault is a common cause defeating the bleed-supplied surface protection across both sides simultaneously (FC-090). The two ice detectors are identical in type - common-mode detection failure could leave icing undetected (FC-087).
praData.mitigation:
Substantiate IPS coverage against the type-design ice envelope; confirm the six independently supplied stabiliser zones and the bleed cross-feed maintain protection under single-source loss; verify shed-ice trajectories do not exceed the engine's ice-ingestion capability nor damage aft structure. Survivability: MINIMISED for accretion by cross-bleed redundancy and independent electrical stabiliser zones (a lost zone is annunciated, SDD 5.10.3); the undetected-loss cases (FC-087, FC-090) and the common-manifold dependency are retained as conditions to be shown acceptable, pending refinement of the preliminary ice envelope.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall maintain protection of the surfaces, inlets and probes within the type-design icing envelope such that no single bleed-manifold or detector common-mode failure results in an undetected loss of protection.
• Ice shed from protected surfaces and inlet cowls shall not exceed the certified engine ice-ingestion capability nor damage aft-fuselage or empennage structure/control runs in zone 800.
aiRequirements: The ice protection system shall maintain protection of the surfaces, inlets and probes within the type-design icing envelope such that no single bleed-manifold or detector common-mode failure results in an undetected loss of protection.
Ice shed from protected surfaces and inlet cowls shall not exceed the certified engine ice-ingestion capability nor damage aft-fuselage or empennage structure/control runs in zone 800.

praData.threat: Cabin / cargo (hold) fire — in-flight fire or overheat in the unoccupied hold or flight-deck / forward equipment bay
praData.desc: Hold fire in a low-differential unoccupied hold (zones 200/300/400) carrying a single unitised blade. Hold has smoke detection at nine stations and NO suppression fitted — a recorded decision the SDD carries forward as an assumption to be substantiated. Fire/overheat in the flight deck (130) or forward equipment bay (120, housing FCC 1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks) is the occupied-zone counterpart. Survivability, not probability: model is at drawing/model stage; hold differential and installation are preliminary and not frozen.
praData.systems: FPR, CRG, FCS, AVI, OXY, HYD
praData.csfl: A hold fire in zone 300 sits at the HV feeder / LV crossing points and at the FCC 2 installation; propagation along the HYD C run (400,300,200), the restraint tension monitoring loop (200,300,400), the low-voltage signal route, and the HV feeder can defeat nominally independent redundancies — FCC 2 (mid bay), HYD C, restraint monitoring, and left/right electrical separation are co-located in the hold and are a common-source candidate. Forward equipment bay (120) co-locates FCC 1, oxygen cylinders and forward avionics; a fire there is a common source across those functions.
praData.mitigation:
Nine-station smoke detection along the hold length (SF-018); dual-loop continuous detection with AND-then-single-loop degradation in engine/APU zones; overheat detection on bleed duct runs and main gear bays; portable extinguishers at flight deck and hold access door; oxygen cylinders installed outside the flight deck and outside any high-energy electrical zone; deliberate no combustible palletised load in the hold. NO fixed hold suppression is fitted — the no-suppression decision is recorded as an assumption requiring substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • The hold-fire safety case shall substantiate the decision to fit hold smoke detection with no fixed suppression, demonstrating survivability of a hold fire against the single-blade / no-palletised-load basis (advisory — review comment).
• The zonal analysis shall examine co-location in zone 300 of FCC 2, the HYD C run, the restraint tension monitoring loop and the HV/LV crossing points against a common hold-fire source, and reflect any common cause in the affected fault trees (advisory).
• Separation / shielding of the forward equipment bay (120) contents — FCC 1, crew-oxygen cylinders and forward avionics — against a local fire source shall be substantiated (advisory).
aiRequirements: The hold-fire safety case shall substantiate the decision to fit hold smoke detection with no fixed suppression, demonstrating survivability of a hold fire against the single-blade / no-palletised-load basis (advisory — review comment).

The zonal analysis shall examine co-location in zone 300 of FCC 2, the HYD C run, the restraint tension monitoring loop and the HV/LV crossing points against a common hold-fire source, and reflect any common cause in the affected fault trees (advisory).
Separation / shielding of the forward equipment bay (120) contents — FCC 1, crew-oxygen cylinders and forward avionics — against a local fire source shall be substantiated (advisory).

praData.threat: Lightning strike (§25.581/§25.1316, AC 20-136B) — direct attachment at extremities and swept-channel to skin, with indirect (conducted/coupled) transients onto wiring
praData.desc: Direct-attachment zones are the extremities/leading edges (wing box & LE 510/520, wing roots 530/540, nacelles 610-640, empennage 800) and the nose visor structure 110 as a forward extremity. Indirect effects (conducted/coupled transients) reach avionics and flight-control electronics in the equipment bays (120 FCC1, 300 FCC2/mid bay, 400 FCC3, 130 flight deck). Failure conditions potentially caused by coupled transients corrupting redundant electronics simultaneously: FCS erroneous/uncommanded axis response FC-014, FC-015, FC-016, FC-017, FC-018, FC-019 and the slow-drift undetected set FC-020, FC-021, FC-022, FC-023; erroneous/undetected flight information FC-016-display family and the FCIM Undetected erroneous flight information (SF-016 Unaware); crew-alerting FC-055-family via AVI. This is a common-cause threat that defeats the three-dissimilar-FCC and dual-network independence claims of SDD §5.3/§5.11 — its impact is CSFL across otherwise-independent FCS/AVI channels.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, PRP (FADEC), IPS (wing anti-ice ducting shares LE with outboard electrical route), FUE (integral wing tanks in direct-attachment zones 510/520)
praData.csfl: Coupled lightning transient corrupting all three dissimilar FCCs and/or both data-network channels simultaneously defeats the FCS/AVI independence claim; direct attachment to a wing-tank zone (510/520) is the fuel-ignition survivability concern
praData.mitigation:
Bond and shield per §25.1316 zoning; airframe as a Faraday enclosure with controlled inter-zone bonding; transient protection at every equipment-bay interface; fuel-system ignition-source elimination in the flammable-fluid wing zones (510/520); the SDD-declared HV/LV route separation (§5.5.5/§5.14.2) and the shielded partition between wing anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route (§5.10.5) — protection LEVELS not yet substantiated, so mitigation is SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE pending §25.1316 test/analysis
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft shall demonstrate that a lightning strike per the §25.1316 zoning cannot simultaneously corrupt all three flight control computers or both data-network channels (protect the FCS/AVI independence claim).
• The fuel system shall demonstrate no ignition source is created in wing zones 510/520 by direct attachment or conducted lightning current (§25.981).
• Indirect-effect transient protection shall be substantiated at every equipment-bay electronic interface (120/300/400/130) to the levels of the §25.1316 environment.
aiRequirements: The aircraft shall demonstrate that a lightning strike per the §25.1316 zoning cannot simultaneously corrupt all three flight control computers or both data-network channels (protect the FCS/AVI independence claim).
The fuel system shall demonstrate no ignition source is created in wing zones 510/520 by direct attachment or conducted lightning current (§25.981).
Indirect-effect transient protection shall be substantiated at every equipment-bay electronic interface (120/300/400/130) to the levels of the §25.1316 environment.

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — pressure boundary when closed, unpressurised when open
zsaData.equip: Visor latches (12 rotary), lock pins (8), lock actuator, sensing harness
zsaData.interference: Lock sensing harness (110→120→130) transits this zone; door actuation power routed opposite side. Common torque-shaft drives all 12 latches — single mechanical common cause. Pressure interlock (<0.1 psi) in series with unlock.
zsaData.mitigation: Two dissimilar independently-routed lock sensing circuits (proximity harness + mechanical linkage/visual indicator); pins on separate hydraulic supply so latches cannot back-drive; pressure interlock. Verify harness/actuation-power separation and the two separated bulkhead penetrations at maintenance.

zsaData.equip: FCC 1, crew oxygen cylinders (2 HP), forward avionics racks, ADIRU
zsaData.interference: Crew O2 cylinders (HP gaseous) co-located with avionics racks and FCC 1 — energetic-vessel rupture adjacent to flight-control computer. LV signal left/right and data network channels 1&2 originate/transit here.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD states cylinders installed outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source and O2 supply line routed clear of HV feeder — CONFIRM against this bay's avionics energy content. Thermal discharge indicator on skin. FCC 1 is 1 of 3 dissimilar computers in separate bays.

zsaData.equip: Displays (4), inceptors, integrated standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks (4)
zsaData.interference: Both nose-door lock sensing paths penetrate the flight-deck bulkhead here at two separated penetrations. Standby instrument shares nothing with primary displays per SDD.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify the two bulkhead penetrations remain separated post-install; standby instrument on DC essential bus on independent route; fire handles/O2 masks accessible from crew stations.

zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3, restraint straps, restraint tension monitoring loop, smoke detectors
zsaData.interference: Restraint tension monitoring loop (single instrumented loop, full hold length, left side above floor) shares this zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (HV feeder + LV signal transit 200). Single-loop coverage is a recorded item.
zsaData.mitigation: Smoke detection at 9 stations (no suppression — recorded assumption to substantiate). Verify separation of tension loop from fuel vent and HV route; loss on two adjacent stations annunciated as restraint condition.

zsaData.desc: Mid hold (stations 4–6) — low differential, unoccupied; principal routing crossover zone
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points
zsaData.interference: HIGH ROUTING DENSITY: HYD A&B share the wing-root run through 300; HYD C, fuel feed gallery, both HV feeders, both LV signals, both data channels, both bleed ducts and the cross-bleed manifold all transit 300; the only two HV↔LV crossing points are here. A+B co-location couples FCs classed Catastrophic (FC-029 loss of attitude control) / Hazardous (FC-026/27/28) — inherited, to be tested by CMA.
zsaData.mitigation: A/B wing-root commonality and the two HV/LV crossing points are recorded installation items requiring CMA. Data channels share no connector/penetration; HV/LV separated except at the two shielded crossing points. FCC 2 is 1 of 3 in separate bays. TEST every A+B independence claim per ARP4761A common-mode.

zsaData.interference: HYD C run (400→300→200), LV signal and data network channels transit 400; restraint tension loop terminates here. FCC 3 housed here — 3rd of the dissimilar computer set.
zsaData.mitigation: FCC 3 in separate bay supporting the 3-computer independence claim; HYD C routed opposite side from A/B. Verify restraint-loop and data-channel separation.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present
zsaData.equip: Fuel tanks (outboard/mid/inboard), cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Wing anti-ice ducting shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route (separated by shielded partition). Fuel tanks co-located with hot bleed ducting and electrical route — flammable-fluid zone with ignition sources present.
zsaData.mitigation: Shielded partition full run between anti-ice duct and electrical route; tank vent/surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses; verify separation and bonding. Bearing PRAs: engine/rotor burst debris, lightning, fuel-tank ignition.

zsaData.desc: Right wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present (mirror of 510)
zsaData.equip: Fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Mirror of 510: anti-ice duct shares leading edge with outboard electrical route behind shielded partition; single pressure refuel/defuel point is in the right wing root — flammable-fluid zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Shielded partition; independent overflow protection on refuel point; tank vents outboard of harnesses. Bearing PRAs: engine/rotor burst, lightning, fuel-tank ignition.

zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: HYD A and B SHARE this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary — the recorded independence claim to be tested. Bleed duct penetration and HV feeder transit co-located at the pressure boundary.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD flags the A/B shared run as a dedicated zonal item; no two hydraulic systems share a wing-root penetration per FCS §5.3.5 (verify vs the shared run statement — apparent tension). Bleed duct kept clear of HV feeder with minimum separation. CMA-critical zone.

zsaData.desc: Right wing root — pressure-boundary transit (mirror of 530)
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: Mirror of 530: shared HYD A/B run across the pressure boundary; bleed duct penetration and HV feeder transit co-located. Fuel feed gallery also transits (510→530→300→540→520).
zsaData.mitigation: A/B shared-run zonal item; HV/bleed minimum separation maintained; fuel gallery physically separated from both hydraulic runs and the HV feeder route per FUE §5.2.5. Verify. CMA-critical.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 (left outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone
zsaData.equip: Engine 1, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Fire zone: high-energy rotating machinery, fuel and hydraulic fluid, generator and EDP co-located. Outboard engine at 28 m moment arm — asymmetric-thrust sizing case. Bleed duct and HV feeder originate here (610→620→530→300→200).
zsaData.mitigation: Dual-loop fire detection routed on opposite sides, AND logic degrading to single-loop; two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed; FADEC dual-channel on independent power. Bearing PRAs: uncontained rotor burst (AC 20-128A), engine burst (§25.901(c)), fire (§25.855), lightning.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 2 (left inboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone
zsaData.equip: Engine 2, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing, thrust reverser
zsaData.interference: Fire zone as 610. Thrust reverser fitted (inboard engines only) — in-flight deployment couples to FC-009 (Catastrophic). Shares extinguisher cross-plumbing with 610.
zsaData.mitigation: WoW + radio-altimeter inhibit and mechanical translating-sleeve lock against in-flight reverser deploy; dual-loop detection; cross-plumbed bottles. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst, engine burst, fire, lightning.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 3 (right inboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone
zsaData.equip: Engine 3, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing, thrust reverser
zsaData.interference: Fire zone; reverser fitted (couples FC-009 Catastrophic). Engine 3 drives HYD B pump — nacelle event affects HYD B source. Shares extinguisher cross-plumbing with 640.
zsaData.mitigation: Reverser in-flight inhibit + mechanical lock; dual-loop detection; cross-plumbed bottles; HYD B has second source (engine 4). Bearing PRAs: rotor burst, engine burst, fire, lightning.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 4 (right outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone
zsaData.equip: Engine 4, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Fire zone as 610. Outboard at 28 m — asymmetric-thrust sizing case. Engine 4 drives HYD B pump and mirrors 610 HV/bleed origination.
zsaData.mitigation: Dual-loop detection opposite-side routed; cross-plumbed bottles; FADEC independent power. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst (AC 20-128A), engine burst, fire, lightning.

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted
zsaData.equip: Three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses
zsaData.interference: Brake hydraulic lines A AND B run through this bay in adjacent (separately clipped) bundles — co-location couples the two braking supplies; recorded zonal item. Carbon brakes are an overheat/fire source in an unpressurised bay.
zsaData.mitigation: A/B brake bundles separately clipped and shielded; overheat detection fitted; steering and braking harnesses on opposite sides of the bay. Bearing PRAs: tire burst / flailing tread (§25.734, AC 25.734-1), brake overheat. TEST A/B adjacency by CMA.

zsaData.desc: Right main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted (mirror of 710)
zsaData.equip: Three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses
zsaData.interference: Mirror of 710: brake lines A and B share the bay in adjacent bundles; carbon-brake overheat source. Brake hydraulic lines A/B routing (710,720,300).
zsaData.mitigation: Separately clipped/shielded A/B bundles; overheat detection; harness separation. Bearing PRAs: tire burst, brake overheat. CMA on A/B adjacency.

zsaData.equip: Nose unit (twin-wheel steerable), steering actuator, tow disconnect
zsaData.interference: Nose steering actuator and tow disconnect co-located; nose unit provides ground directional control and part of ground support.
zsaData.mitigation: Mechanical disconnect for towing; free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure; dual downlock proximity sensing. Bearing PRAs: tire burst.

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed environment; APU compartment is a fire zone
zsaData.equip: Rudder control runs (upper/lower segments), stabiliser heater feeders, APU compartment
zsaData.interference: APU compartment is a fire zone within a mixed zone. Upper/lower rudder control runs on opposite sides of the aft fuselage; stabiliser heater feeders routed opposite side from rudder runs. LV signal and data channels transit 800.
zsaData.mitigation: Rudder segment runs and stabiliser feeders on opposite sides; APU dual-loop detection with dedicated bottle auto-discharged unattended and automatic shutdown/fuel isolation on APU fire. Bearing PRAs: APU/engine burst, fire. Verify rudder-run separation.

cmaData.subject: G-006 Elevator actuation independence — HYD A vs HYD C
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: HYD A and HYD C provide independent motive power to the elevators such that no single cause disables both supplies.. Elevator actuation is independent because it is supplied from hydraulic systems A and C, which are entirely separate in fluid, pumping and distribution.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — HYD C is pumped by AC electric motor pumps with a RAT emergency source; loss of all AC generation drives C onto the RAT, an exposure not shared with engine-driven HYD A (contributor: common AC-generation loss coupling C's availability). Installation Design — SDD records A and B (not A and C) sharing a wing-root run; HYD system C is routed separately along the opposite side, which supports A/C physical independence. Environment/Implementation — both A and C actuators act on the common elevator surfaces and their shared attachment/hinge structure; a surface or dual-actuator installation common cause (jam, structural) defeats the actuation claim regardless of supply independence (elevator surface is a structural/PRA item). No shared reservoir or fluid path (systems cannot transfer fluid).
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain HYD A engine-driven and HYD C electric/RAT dissimilar sourcing; verify HYD C routing remains segregated from HYD A per §5.4.5; confirm elevator dual-actuator/surface common-cause (jam) is addressed by FCS design and Particular Risk / structural substantiation; verify DC-essential/RAT availability keeps HYD C pressurised under total AC loss.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• HYD A and HYD C supplies to the elevators shall share no reservoir, pump drive, electrical source or routing that could constitute a single common cause.
• The elevator actuation installation shall preclude a single mechanical common cause (jam, structural failure of shared attachment) disabling both A- and C-supplied actuators.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/SSA verification: confirm as-built HYD C routing separation from HYD A, confirm RAT/electric-pump availability under total AC loss, and confirm elevator surface/actuator common-cause is dispositioned by structural analysis and PRA before crediting the A/C AND gate.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: HYD A and HYD C provide independent motive power to the elevators such that no single cause disables both supplies.
aiRequirements: HYD A and HYD C supplies to the elevators shall share no reservoir, pump drive, electrical source or routing that could constitute a single common cause.
The elevator actuation installation shall preclude a single mechanical common cause (jam, structural failure of shared attachment) disabling both A- and C-supplied actuators.
cmaData.aiVerification: ASA/SSA verification: confirm as-built HYD C routing separation from HYD A, confirm RAT/electric-pump availability under total AC loss, and confirm elevator surface/actuator common-cause is dispositioned by structural analysis and PRA before crediting the A/C AND gate.

cmaData.subject: G-007 FCC command-path independence — three dissimilar flight control computers
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: FCC 1, FCC 2 and FCC 3 fail independently such that no single cause defeats the voted command path.. The stabiliser/elevator command path is independent because three dissimilar flight control computers vote on command, each from a different electrical source, in three separate bays.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design — dissimilar hardware and software developed by one of TWO teams under a dissimilarity argument; with three computers and only two software teams at least two channels share a code baseline, and a common REQUIREMENTS/specification error is common to all three regardless of coding team (contributor: common specification/requirement error defeating the vote). Installation Design — computers in three separate bays (forward, mid, aft equipment bays), electrically supplied from different sources — supports physical and power independence. Common Resources — command path relies on the dual deterministic data network and on shared air-data/inertial inputs; a common external input error or common-mode ADIRU error can drive all three to an erroneous voted output (relevant to erroneous-command trees; for LOSS the network loss is dual-channel). Environment — three bays in different zones reduce shared thermal/EMI exposure.
cmaData.mitigation:
Maintain three-bay physical and power separation; strengthen the dissimilarity argument to cover the two-team software allocation across three channels; verify requirements-error mitigation (independent validation of the command specification) since specification error is not covered by coding dissimilarity; verify dual-network and multi-ADIRU independence feeding the FCCs.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCC dissimilarity argument shall demonstrate that the two-team software allocation across three channels does not create a common software fault defeating the vote.
• A common requirements/specification error shall not be capable of producing a coincident erroneous or lost command across all three FCCs; independent specification validation shall be evidenced.
• FCC 1/2/3 electrical supplies and bay installations shall remain segregated such that no single power or zonal event disables more than one FCC.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/SSA verification: confirm as-built three-bay separation, distinct electrical sources per FCC, and the software/requirements dissimilarity case; confirm this independence underpins any DAL reduction on the command path (App P) and that its failure would invalidate that reduction.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: FCC 1, FCC 2 and FCC 3 fail independently such that no single cause defeats the voted command path.
aiRequirements: The FCC dissimilarity argument shall demonstrate that the two-team software allocation across three channels does not create a common software fault defeating the vote.
A common requirements/specification error shall not be capable of producing a coincident erroneous or lost command across all three FCCs; independent specification validation shall be evidenced.
FCC 1/2/3 electrical supplies and bay installations shall remain segregated such that no single power or zonal event disables more than one FCC.
cmaData.aiVerification: ASA/SSA verification: confirm as-built three-bay separation, distinct electrical sources per FCC, and the software/requirements dissimilarity case; confirm this independence underpins any DAL reduction on the command path (App P) and that its failure would invalidate that reduction.

cmaData.subject: G-008 Pitch-control independence — actuation AND command AND mechanical reversion
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim is independent of the FBW actuation and command paths, so no single cause defeats all three.. Complete loss of pitch control requires the coincident loss of elevator/stabiliser actuation, the three-FCC command path, AND the mechanical reversion path to the stabiliser trim.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design — mechanical reversion is dissimilar by nature (no software, no FCC, no command-path electronics), which is the strongest independence in the set and defends the AND. Common Resources — reversion is to the stabiliser trim; the trimmable horizontal stabiliser and elevators act on the same tail structure, so a common structural / installation event in the empennage (zone 800) could couple the FBW pitch surfaces and the reversion path (contributor: common empennage structural / zonal event — a Particular Risk / structural item). Installation — the pitch actuation depends on HYD A/C and the reversion path is mechanical; verify the reversion linkage routing does not share a zone hazard with the elevator actuation such that one event takes both. Operation — reversion results from loss of all electrical command paths and is not a selectable mode; its availability assumes the mechanical path is maintained/rigged correctly (common maintenance/rigging error is a credible common cause across the reversion linkage). Data — no failure rate asserted; quantification of the AND is the engine's.
cmaData.mitigation:
Preserve mechanical reversion as a dissimilar, non-electrical path; verify empennage zonal/particular-risk analysis (zone 800) does not present a single event defeating both FBW pitch surfaces and the reversion linkage; control common maintenance/rigging error on the reversion path via independent inspection; confirm reversion linkage routing separated from elevator actuation.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim shall share no electrical source, hydraulic source, software or command electronics with the FBW pitch actuation and command paths.
• No single empennage structural or zonal event shall be capable of simultaneously defeating the elevator/stabiliser FBW actuation and the mechanical reversion path.
• Maintenance/rigging of the mechanical reversion path shall be subject to independent verification to preclude a common human-error common cause.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/SSA verification: confirm the reversion path's physical and functional dissimilarity as built, confirm empennage Particular Risk / zonal analysis addresses the common structural event, and confirm the reversion path availability is not credited without maintenance-error mitigation before accepting the top pitch AND gate.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim is independent of the FBW actuation and command paths, so no single cause defeats all three.
aiRequirements: The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim shall share no electrical source, hydraulic source, software or command electronics with the FBW pitch actuation and command paths.
No single empennage structural or zonal event shall be capable of simultaneously defeating the elevator/stabiliser FBW actuation and the mechanical reversion path.

cmaData.subject: Independence of aileron actuation supplies HYD B and HYD C (node 25, under Loss of roll control)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Redundant hydraulic supply: ailerons driven by two actuators on different hydraulic systems (B and C), each system separate in fluid, pumping and distribution.. The two aileron actuators per surface, supplied from HYD B and HYD C respectively, fail independently so that loss of aileron actuation requires loss of both HYD B and HYD C.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: HYD C is pumped by two AC electric-motor pumps with a RAT backstop, so HYD C availability depends on AC generation; HYD B is engine-driven (engines 3,4) — the two are not driven from a common source, supporting independence. Installation Design: SDD states HYD C is 'Routed separately from A and B along the opposite side' (§4 routing), so B and C do not share the aileron-relevant wing-root run; the A/B shared wing-root run does not couple B and C. Environment: aileron actuators for a surface are co-located at that surface — a single mechanical/thermal or particular-risk event at the surface could strike both actuator supplies at that point; not resolved by system-level separation. Development/Design: hydraulic component commonality across systems not described.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain HYD B (engine-driven) vs HYD C (electric+RAT) source dissimilarity as the primary independence basis. Verify actuator-level physical separation at each aileron surface so a single local event does not sever both B and C feeds. Confirm HYD B and HYD C do not converge in any shared bay or penetration near the aileron.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The HYD B and HYD C feeds to each aileron actuator shall be physically separated at the surface such that no single local mechanical, thermal, or debris event severs both supplies.
• The HYD C electric-motor-pump AC source and the HYD B engine-driven source shall share no common electrical bus whose loss disables both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-installed separation of B and C aileron feeds at the surface and to verify no shared AC bus couples HYD C pumps to HYD B pumping; close against ZSA for the aileron zone.

cmaData.subject: Independence of the three flight control computers in the aileron/spoiler roll command path (node 28)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Triple dissimilar FCC redundancy: three flight control computers voting on command, each from a different electrical source, with software dissimilarity.. The three FCCs generate roll commands independently so that loss of the command path requires all three FCCs to fail.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: each FCC 'is supplied from a different electrical source' (§5.3.2), supporting supply independence. Development/Design (software): dissimilarity is claimed but 'hosts software developed by one of two teams' — three computers over only two software teams means at least two FCCs may share a software team, a residual common-design/common-error contributor not eliminated by the triplex vote. Installation Design: the three FCCs are in three separate bays — FCC 1 forward equipment bay (zone 120), FCC 2 mid equipment bay (zone 300), FCC 3 aft equipment bay (zone 400) — supporting physical separation. Common Resources (data/input): a common erroneous air-data/inertial input feeding all three FCCs could defeat the vote (see the tree's own common-mode leaf 162 'Common-mode FCC command error defeats voting'). Environment: no single zone houses more than one FCC.
cmaData.mitigation:
Preserve three-bay physical separation and independent electrical sourcing. Address the two-team software commonality: identify which FCC pair shares a team and argue or bound the common-mode software error, or introduce dissimilar design assurance per DO-178C. Ensure input voting/monitoring detects a common erroneous air-data/inertial source before it is voted through.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCC software dissimilarity argument shall demonstrate that no common software error can produce a coincident erroneous roll command across the voting set, given only two development teams for three computers.
• The roll command voting/monitoring shall detect and reject a common erroneous air-data or inertial input before it is accepted by the voted command path.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to review the software dissimilarity evidence (team allocation, dissimilar design assurance) and to verify the input-monitor coverage for common-mode air-data/inertial errors; confirm the three-bay separation as installed.

cmaData.subject: Independence of the roll-control loss contributors (node 24: aileron actuation AND aileron/spoiler command path)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Roll redundancy composed of independent hydraulic actuation (HYD B/C) and independent triplex FCC command, plus multi-function spoilers as an additional roll effector.. Loss of aileron actuation and loss of the aileron/spoiler command path are independent, so complete loss of roll control requires both.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: the command path and the actuation path both ultimately depend on electrical power — FCCs on three sources and HYD C on AC generation; a wide electrical-generation loss is a shared cause that could degrade both branches concurrently (RAT/emergency generator backstops the essential set). Installation Design: roll effectors (ailerons + multi-function spoilers) and their supplies span the wings; a wing-region particular risk could affect actuation and spoiler branches together. Development/Design: FCC two-team software commonality (node 28) and any hydraulic component commonality (node 25) are inherited common-cause contributors to this higher AND. Environment: no single bay houses both the full actuation and full command paths, but the mid equipment bay (zone 300) is the principal routing crossover zone and hosts FCC 2 plus HV/LV crossing points — a zone 300 event is a candidate common contributor to be examined.
cmaData.mitigation:
Carry the lower-level common-cause contributors (FCC software commonality; HYD B/C surface co-location; shared AC dependency of HYD C) explicitly into this tree rather than relying on the composite AND. Examine zone 300 as a common-cause zone for the roll command path (FCC 2 + HV/LV crossings). Rely on spoiler roll augmentation and mechanical-reversion context where credited.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The roll-control independence case shall model the shared electrical-generation dependency of the FCC command path and the HYD C actuation branch as an explicit common-cause contributor.
• Zone 300 shall be assessed under ZSA for a single event affecting FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points that could couple the roll command path.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the roll top-event fault tree includes explicit common-cause contributors for shared AC dependency and zone-300 co-location, and to close them against the ZSA and electrical-power SSA.

cmaData.subject: Loss of lower rudder segment actuation AND mechanical reversion (G-012, page node 34) — independence of HYD B supply vs mechanical reversion path
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the HYD B hydraulic supply to the lower rudder and the mechanical reversion path to the same segment.. (2) Installation/Environment — co-location: both the lower-segment hydraulic actuation and the mechanical reversion run terminate at the lower rudder in zone 800 | a single zonal event (fire/APU-compartment, node in zone 800) could strike both physical paths at the segment | SDD §3 zone 800 'APU is a fire zone'; rudder control runs routed zone 800. cmaData.subject: Loss of yaw control (G-013, page node 32) — independence of upper rudder (HYD A) vs lower rudder (HYD B) segments
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between HYD A (upper rudder segment) and HYD B (lower rudder segment) supplies underpinning the split-rudder yaw redundancy.. Complete loss of yaw control requires loss of the upper rudder segment (HYD A, node 33) AND loss of the lower rudder segment actuation (node 34); the two segments and their hydraulic supplies are asserted independent.
cmaData.findings: VERIFICATION phase (ASA). Table M2 for the principle 'HYD A upper-rudder independent of HYD B lower-rudder': | Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence | (1) Common Resources — hydraulic routing: SDD §5.4.5 records that systems A and B SHARE a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (zones 530/540) | a single event in that shared wing-root run could deplete or contaminate both A and B, defeating the yaw AND gate directly | SDD §5.4.5 'Systems A and B nonetheless share a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary'; recorded as a dedicated zonal item — must be modelled as a common-cause contributor to node 32, not left as a clean AND. (2) Installation — the rudder control runs are on opposite sides of aft fuselage (zone 800), supporting segment separation | supports independence of the control runs | SDD §5.3.5 'Rudder control runs to the upper and lower segments are routed on opposite sides of the aft fuselage'. (3) Common Development/Design — A and B are separate hydraulic systems, separate reservoir/pump/return | supports resource independence away from the wing root | SDD §5.4.2 'Systems A, B and C are entirely separate in fluid, pumping and distribution'. Net: the shared wing-root run (530/540) is a credible common cause against the HYD A / HYD B independence claim in this gate.

cmaData.subject: Complete loss of attitude control about three axes (G-014, page node 14) — independence across pitch, roll and yaw control
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence across the three control axes — three FCCs (dissimilar software, separate bays, separate electrical sources) and three hydraulic systems distributed so no single resource takes all three axes.. The Catastrophic top event (FC-029) requires simultaneous loss of pitch (node 15), roll (node 24) AND yaw (node 32) control; the three axes, three flight control computers, three hydraulic systems and dissimilar FCC software are asserted independent.
cmaData.findings: VERIFICATION phase (ASA). Table M2 for the principle 'pitch, roll, yaw axes independent to the three-axis AND': | Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence | (1) Common Resources — hydraulic distribution: pitch=A+C, roll=B+C, yaw=A+B; HYD C is common to pitch and roll, HYD A common to pitch and yaw, HYD B common to roll and yaw | no single hydraulic system loss takes all three axes (each axis has two supplies), so the three-axis AND is not defeated by one system; BUT the A/B shared wing-root run (§5.4.5) couples yaw (A+B) and contributes to roll(B)/pitch(A) — a wing-root event degrades multiple axes simultaneously | SDD §5.3.2 'the rudder segments are supplied from systems A and B; the elevators from A and C; the ailerons from B and C'; §5.4.5 shared A/B run. (2) Common Development/Design — three FCCs, dissimilar software from two teams, three separate bays (fwd/mid/aft equipment bays), each on a different electrical source | supports FCC independence; residual common-mode is the shared voting/command architecture and any common specification error across all three | SDD §5.3.2 'three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command ... software developed by one of two teams under a dissimilarity argument'; §5.3.5 'three separate bays'. Note two teams for three computers means at least two FCCs share a software team — a common software error could take that pair. (3) Common Resources — electrical: FCCs on different sources; DC essential is the final resort feeding FCCs, standby, engine controls | loss of DC essential is a candidate common cause across command paths | SDD §5.5.2 'the flight control computers ... are all supplied from it'. (4) Installation/Environment — FCC 2 sits in mid hold (zone 300), the principal routing crossover zone where HV/LV cross and A/B/C-related runs transit | a zone-300 event is a co-location concern for command-path and hydraulic-transit elements | SDD §3 zone 300 'HV/LV crossing points'; §5.5.5 HV/LV cross at two points in mid equipment bay.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify (a) the two-team/three-FCC dissimilarity argument bounds common software error such that no single specification/software fault fails the voting set; (b) DC-essential-bus loss does not simultaneously fail the command paths credited independent; (c) zone 300 (mid hold, crossover) and the A/B wing-root run are covered by ZSA so no single zonal event degrades the required multi-axis set; carry the A/B wing-root commonality as an explicit common-cause contributor. Any principle that fails here invalidates the DAL-A reduction resting on it (ARP4754B App P).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The three flight control computers shall be shown, by dissimilarity and independence argument, such that no single software or specification error can fail the voting set.
• The three-axis attitude-control fault tree shall carry the HYD A/B shared wing-root run and any DC-essential-bus common supply as explicit common-cause contributors rather than a clean three-way AND.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA review of the FCC dissimilarity argument against ARP4754B App P; ZSA of zones 300, 530/540 and 800; confirmation that the fault tree node 14 and its yaw sub-tree carry the identified common-cause couplings; reconcile with EPS DC-essential common-supply analysis.

cmaData.subject: G-015/G-016 — Both downlock sensing circuits indicate locked despite an unlocked gear unit (FC-037, page Erroneous downlock indication presented, node 39 AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent dual downlock sensing — two independent proximity circuits per unit. The two independent downlock proximity sensing circuits per gear unit fail-to-'locked' independently, so a false down-and-locked indication requires two independent circuit failures (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Design: the SDD states downlock is sensed by two proximity circuits that are 'independent' but of like type — a common design/part-number and common sensing principle can drive both to the same false-positive failure mode, and node 42 (Common-mode failure of both proximity sensors) already carries this in the tree. | Common Installation/Environment: both circuits sense the same gear unit within the same gear bay (zones 710/720/730, unpressurised, overheat detection fitted); a bay-local environment (heat, contamination, vibration, mechanical damage) can bias both to read 'engaged'. | Common Maintenance: identical proximity circuits invite the same calibration/rigging action, a credible common-cause. | This principle underpins the DAL-A allocation on FC-037; if the two circuits are not genuinely independent the AND at node 39 overstates protection.
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate dissimilarity or staggered maintenance/calibration between the two proximity circuits; retain node 42 as an explicit common-cause contributor rather than a pure AND; apply zonal (ZSA) separation and shielding within the gear bay so a single bay event cannot bias both circuits.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two downlock proximity sensing circuits per gear unit shall be shown to fail to a 'locked' indication independently, with any common-mode failure explicitly modelled as a separate contributor.
• Downlock sensing calibration/rigging actions shall be defined so that a single maintenance error cannot bias both circuits of a unit to false-locked.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA to confirm the as-built dual downlock sensing retains an explicit common-cause contributor (node 42) and that zonal/maintenance mitigations are in place; verify against the ZSA for zones 710/720/730.

cmaData.subject: G-020 — Complete loss of ground support of the aircraft: left main-gear AND right main-gear AND nose-unit support all lost (FC-040, page Complete loss of ground support, node 43 AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent multi-unit ground support — six main bogies (three per side) plus nose unit. The left main-gear, right main-gear and nose-unit support functions fail independently, so complete loss of ground support requires simultaneous independent loss of all three (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource: retraction/extension of all units is by hydraulic system A with a free-fall alternate; a single HYD A failure coupled with a free-fall failure is a shared cause across the not-down-and-locked branches (nodes 46, 49, 52), so those branches are not fully independent of one another. | Common Design: each unit's down-and-locked state relies on the same downlock design/sensing philosophy, a common-design contributor across left, right and nose branches. | Common Environment/Structure: the semi-prepared-surface flotation and 318 t landing-weight case is a shared structural/environmental stressor acting on all bogies simultaneously (the flotation design is common to every unit); a single surface/overload event can act on multiple units, weakening the independence of the structural-collapse branches (nodes 45, 48, 51). | This principle underpins the DAL-A allocation on FC-040; a shared HYD A/free-fall or common flotation cause invalidates the optimism of the three-way AND.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the shared HYD A extension path (and free-fall alternate) as an explicit common-cause contributor rather than relying on a pure AND across the not-down-and-locked branches; substantiate that structural collapse of the units is driven by independent load paths (PRA/ZSA for tyre-burst and semi-prepared-surface overload); confirm the free-fall alternate is independent of hydraulic pressure per the SDD.

• Loss of all three gear-support units (left main, right main, nose) shall be shown not to arise from a single shared cause — in particular the HYD A extension path, its free-fall alternate, or a common downlock design.
• The common semi-prepared-surface flotation and maximum-landing-weight case shall be assessed as a shared structural stressor across all bogies, with independence of the structural load paths substantiated.
