1) Common torque-shaft drive (Common Resources / mechanical) | Already a repeated basic under the latch branch; if it also back-drives or shares drive with pins, defeats the AND | SDD states pins driven by separate actuator on separate supply so latches cannot back-drive while pins engaged — coupling limited but torque-shaft is a single point for all twelve latches
2) Shared hydraulic supply (Common Resources / hydraulic) | Latch drive on system A (visor drive), lock pin actuator on a 'separate supply' — if the separate supply is derived from the same source, a single hydraulic loss disables both | SDD: 'Eight independent locking pins ... driven ... by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply' — separateness asserted but source not identified; requires verification
3) Co-location in zone 110 (Installation Design / Environment) | Latches, lock pins, lock actuator and sensing harness all in the nose visor structure; a single zonal event (impact, fire, structural distortion on visor) strikes both sets | Zone 110 is the pressure boundary when closed and unpressurised when open; no separation possible between latch and pin sets within one door
4) Common maintenance / rigging action (Maintenance) | A single mis-rig of the latch/pin mechanism on turnaround defeats both | Operating concept assumes no line maintenance at strip; both sectors dispatched from origin — a single origin action affects both
cmaData.mitigation: Confirm the lock-pin actuator hydraulic supply is sourced independently of the visor-drive supply (system A); if not, add a common hydraulic-supply basic event under the gate. Retain the common torque-shaft as a repeated event / dedicated common-cause contributor. Substantiate zone-110 particular-risk and zonal coverage so a single door-structure event is not credible against both latch and pin sets. Impose a rigging/verification independence requirement so a single maintenance action cannot mis-set both.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Latch set and pin set are separately driven (latches on a common torque shaft; pins driven by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply) so no single cause disables both.

cmaData.subject: G-033 Loss of both straps at a saddle station — independence of strap 1 vs strap 2 at one saddle
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Each saddle carries two independent tension straps, electric-winch tensioned and mechanically locked, so a single failure loses only one strap.. The two tension straps at a single saddle station fail independently, so loss of both straps at one station requires two independent failures (AND gate, node 88).
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1) Common CRG electrical supply to winches (Common Resources / electrical) | Both straps at a station are tensioned by electric winches consuming CRG power; a single power loss slackens both | SDD: CRG 'Consumes EPS'; both winches at one saddle likely on the same feed — requires verification of per-strap feed separation
2) Single tension monitoring loop (Common Resources / data) | Loss of the single instrumented loop removes detection for both straps at the station, so a developing dual-strap loss is not annunciated | SDD: 'single instrumented loop ... coverage is a recorded item' — monitoring is common to both straps, not a restraint load path itself
3) Co-location at one saddle / same hold station (Installation Design / Environment) | Both straps share the saddle, its hard-point pin and conforming interface; a single saddle-structure or hard-point failure defeats both | SDD: 'There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points' — hard-point loss is a separate single-point already, but saddle geometry loss defeats the strap pair
4) Common winch/strap part and rigging (Development/Design; Maintenance) | Identical strap and winch parts, tensioned by the same ground procedure, share a common design or mis-tension cause | Loading is a single ground procedure per §5.8.6; a single mis-set at loading affects both straps at a station
cmaData.mitigation: Verify the two winches at each saddle are fed from separate CRG electrical feeds; if common, add a shared-supply basic event under the gate. Treat the single tension monitoring loop as a common detection contributor (its loss defeats the compensating annunciation, not the restraint itself). Substantiate hold-zone particular-risk/zonal coverage so a single station event is not credible against both straps. Impose a loading-procedure independence requirement so a single mis-tension does not set both straps below load.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Each saddle carries two independent tension straps, electric-winch tensioned and mechanically locked, so a single failure loses only one strap.

cmaData.subject: G-034 Combined multi-station strap loss — independence of one station's strap loss vs the adjacent station's strap loss
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Load paths are sized so the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours; loss at adjacent stations simultaneously is treated as requiring independent events at each station.. Strap loss at one saddle station and strap loss at the adjacent station fail independently, so a combined multi-station loss defeating neighbour load-sharing requires independent failures at each station (AND gate, node 87).
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1) Single spanwise restraint tension monitoring loop (Common Resources / data) | One instrumented loop runs the full hold length; its loss removes annunciation across all stations, so an undetected loss can accumulate across adjacent stations before the crew reacts | SDD: 'single instrumented loop ... full hold length' and 'loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition' — the annunciation itself depends on the shared loop
2) Common CRG electrical supply along the left hold side (Common Resources / electrical) | The tension loop and left-side electrical route run the hold length; a single supply/route event affects winches and monitoring at multiple stations | SDD: loop 'shares the hold zone with the fuel gallery vent and with the left-side electrical route; that shared zone is a recorded item'
3) Shared hold zone / spanwise event (Installation Design / Environment) | A single spanwise event (shift of the blade, structural distortion, impact) acts on adjacent saddles together, defeating the neighbour load-sharing assumption | Stations 1–9 are distributed across zones 200/300/400 — spanwise separation exists but a single blade shift couples adjacent stations mechanically
4) Common design / loading procedure across stations (Development/Design; Operational) | Identical saddle/strap design and one loading procedure across all stations means a systematic mis-tension can affect several adjacent stations at once | Single ground loading procedure per §5.8.6; a systematic error is not confined to one station
cmaData.mitigation: Model the single tension monitoring loop as a common detection contributor across all stations (its loss undermines the adjacent-station annunciation that G-034 relies on for timely detection). Verify hold-length electrical feed separation so a single left-side route event does not disable multiple stations. Substantiate the blade-shift / spanwise particular-risk so a single mechanical event is not credible against adjacent stations. Impose a loading-procedure independence requirement so a systematic mis-tension cannot span adjacent stations undetected.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Load paths are sized so the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours; loss at adjacent stations simultaneously is treated as requiring independent events at each station.

cmaData.subject: G-037 — Erroneous data not detected (standby + comparator independent of primary error source)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Detection independence: standby instrument shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays; comparator is an independent monitor.. The independent standby instrument and the alerting comparator detect erroneous primary flight information, so a primary-chain error and its non-detection are independent (AND-gate node 96, page-1788050493420-994).
cmaData.findings: COMMON RESOURCES / power: the SDD supplies ADIRU 3 AND the integrated standby instrument from the DC essential bus, and the primary chain's essential path also lands on that bus. Loss of, or a fault on, the DC essential bus is a shared cause that can remove the very standby the AND relies on for detection — belongs in the tree as a common-cause contributor, not left implicit. COMMON DESIGN / sensor: standby claims 'shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays' — a genuine dissimilarity that supports the AND if verified as built. COMMON EXTERNAL INPUT: gate G-038 already captures a common external / common-mode ADIRU error upstream; if the standby draws air-data from a source correlated with the primary pitot/static, the comparator cannot reveal it. Verification must confirm the standby's sensing is physically and functionally independent of the primary air-data set.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm and document the standby instrument's supply/sensor/processing independence per SDD 5.11.3/5.11.5; treat DC essential bus as an explicit common-cause contributor combined with the detection logic; verify the alerting comparator is powered/processed independently of the primary display chain.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The standby flight instrument shall share no electrical supply, no sensor and no signal-processing element with the primary flight and navigation display chain.
• The alerting comparator that flags inconsistent primary flight information shall be powered and processed independently of the primary display processing units it monitors.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/SSA to verify as-built independence of standby supply/sensor/processing; wiring-route and bus-allocation inspection confirming DC essential bus dependency is modeled as a common-cause contributor; ZSA reconciliation for forward equipment bay (zone 120) / flight deck (zone 130) co-location.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Detection independence: standby instrument shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays; comparator is an independent monitor.
aiRequirements: The standby flight instrument shall share no electrical supply, no sensor and no signal-processing element with the primary flight and navigation display chain.
The alerting comparator that flags inconsistent primary flight information shall be powered and processed independently of the primary display processing units it monitors.
cmaData.aiVerification: ASA/SSA to verify as-built independence of standby supply/sensor/processing; wiring-route and bus-allocation inspection confirming DC essential bus dependency is modeled as a common-cause contributor; ZSA reconciliation for forward equipment bay (zone 120) / flight deck (zone 130) co-location.

cmaData.subject: G-038 — Erroneous flight information consistent across sources undetected (top AND node 92)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Source/detection independence: a common-mode input error is only hazardous if simultaneously undetected; the two branches are asserted independent.. An erroneous-flight-information source and the failure of all detection means are independent events, so their conjunction (AND-gate node 92, page-1788050493420-994) is the credible path to undetected erroneous information.
cmaData.findings: COMMON EXTERNAL INPUT: the error branch (node 93) explicitly admits a 'common external input error affecting all sources' and a 'common-mode ADIRU error (common part number)' — the three ADIRUs are of common type, so a common design/sensor deficiency defeats source diversity. COMMON DESIGN: ADIRU common part number is a design-level common-cause contributor already surfaced under the error branch; it must not ALSO be double-counted in the detection branch. DETECTION independence: the non-detection branch (node 96) depends on the standby instrument and the comparator; per the DC-essential-bus finding on G-037, a bus fault can couple the source path and the detection path, weakening the claim that node 93 and node 96 are independent. INSTALLATION: display processors in three separate bays and dual network channels on opposite sides (SDD 5.11.5) support diversity for equipment faults but not for a common upstream air-data/ADIRU error.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the common-type ADIRU error and the common external-input error as explicit common-cause contributors under the source branch; verify the detection branch (standby + comparator) does not share the DC essential bus fault path with the source branch such that one event fails both; substantiate ADIRU dissimilarity or add an independent air-data monitor.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The undetected-erroneous-information condition shall model common part-number ADIRU error and common external-input error as explicit common-cause contributors under the source branch of the fault tree.
• The detection means for erroneous primary flight information shall not share a single failure (including DC essential bus loss) that simultaneously produces the erroneous information.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/SSA review confirming common-cause contributors are represented in the tree (not left as an optimistic AND); dissimilarity argument for the three ADIRUs assessed; independence of source vs detection power/data paths verified against EWS routing (data channels 1/2 opposite sides, no shared connector).
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Source/detection independence: a common-mode input error is only hazardous if simultaneously undetected; the two branches are asserted independent.
aiRequirements: The undetected-erroneous-information condition shall model common part-number ADIRU error and common external-input error as explicit common-cause contributors under the source branch of the fault tree.
The detection means for erroneous primary flight information shall not share a single failure (including DC essential bus loss) that simultaneously produces the erroneous information.
cmaData.aiVerification: ASA/SSA review confirming common-cause contributors are represented in the tree (not left as an optimistic AND); dissimilarity argument for the three ADIRUs assessed; independence of source vs detection power/data paths verified against EWS routing (data channels 1/2 opposite sides, no shared connector).

cmaData.subject: G-039 — Loss of all three display processing units (independent failure of DPU 1/2/3)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Redundancy independence of three identical active processing units installed in three separate bays.. Display processing units 1, 2 and 3 fail independently, so their simultaneous loss (AND-gate node 101, page-1788050493430-380) is the credible path to loss of all primary display processing.
cmaData.findings: COMMON DESIGN / identical active redundancy: three DPUs are redundant identical active components — per NASA-FTH common-cause guidance a common-cause contribution should be included for any redundancy of identical active components as the count grows; a shared design or software defect can disable all three. This shared cause is not captured by the plain AND and must be added as an explicit common-cause contributor. COMMON RESOURCES / network: the DPUs drive the displays on a 'dual redundant deterministic data network'; the SDD does not state whether the three DPUs share a processing/network resource beyond the dual channels — verification must confirm no shared network or power element defeats the three-way independence. INSTALLATION: the SDD places 'the three display processors in three separate bays' (forward/mid/aft equipment bays, zones 120/300/400), giving good physical/zonal separation against a single local event. ENVIRONMENT: separate bays mitigate a common thermal/mechanical/fire environment, but a common HIRF/lightning coupling on a shared data network path is not excluded by the text. SOFTWARE: dissimilarity is stated for the flight control computers, NOT asserted for the DPUs — common software across the three DPUs is a credible common-cause contributor to assess.
cmaData.mitigation:
Add an explicit common-cause contributor for the three identical DPUs (common design/software/manufacturing lot) combined with the independent-failure AND; verify separate power sources and no shared network/processing resource across DPU 1/2/3; assess DPU software dissimilarity or common-mode software error; confirm zonal separation (zones 120/300/400) via ZSA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fault tree for loss of all three display processing units shall include an explicit common-cause contributor for the three identical active display processing units (common design, software and manufacturing lot).
• Display processing units 1, 2 and 3 shall be verified to share no single power source, network element or processing resource whose loss disables all three.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ASA/SSA verification that a DPU common-cause contributor is modeled (identical active redundancy per NASA-FTH); bay-allocation and EWS routing inspection confirming three-bay separation and independent supplies; DPU software commonality assessment; ZSA for zones 120/300/400 confirming no single zonal event takes all three.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Redundancy independence of three identical active processing units installed in three separate bays.
aiRequirements: The fault tree for loss of all three display processing units shall include an explicit common-cause contributor for the three identical active display processing units (common design, software and manufacturing lot).
Display processing units 1, 2 and 3 shall be verified to share no single power source, network element or processing resource whose loss disables all three.
cmaData.aiVerification: ASA/SSA verification that a DPU common-cause contributor is modeled (identical active redundancy per NASA-FTH); bay-allocation and EWS routing inspection confirming three-bay separation and independent supplies; DPU software commonality assessment; ZSA for zones 120/300/400 confirming no single zonal event takes all three.

cmaData.subject: Four display units — independence of the redundant display set (G-040)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the four display units. The four display units fail independently, so complete loss requires all four to fail (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (electrical): DU set draws on main and essential supplies — a bus/feeder loss common to the set defeats independence [Effect: collapses the AND | Mitigating: primary displays fed from main AND essential feeds, but supply commonality not enumerated per-DU]. Development/Design: four DUs are a single part number / common software and format engine — a common design or software defect fails all four simultaneously [Effect: common-mode of the whole set | Mitigating: 'Any display unit can present any format' implies identical build — no dissimilarity claimed]. Common Resource (data): all DUs fed by the same three display processors and dual network — upstream fault presents to all four (captured separately by G-041/DPU gate). Installation: DUs co-located on the flight deck (zone 130) — a zonal event (smoke, fire, HIRF ingress) strikes the set together. Excluded as not credible: common manufacturing lot treated under design commonality; maintenance calibration N/A to passive displays.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence of the four DUs rests on the independent standby instrument, which 'shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays' — the standby is the dissimilar backstop, not the DU redundancy itself. Model DU common part-number/software as an explicit common-cause contributor under G-040 rather than a pure AND.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The four display units shall not share a single electrical supply path such that one feeder loss fails the redundant set.
• A common design/software defect in the display units shall be mitigated by the dissimilar independent standby instrument, whose independence shall be verified.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm per-DU supply segregation and add a common-cause contributor (common part number / common software) to G-040; confirm standby-instrument independence closes the residual.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the four display units
aiRequirements: The four display units shall not share a single electrical supply path such that one feeder loss fails the redundant set.
A common design/software defect in the display units shall be mitigated by the dissimilar independent standby instrument, whose independence shall be verified.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm per-DU supply segregation and add a common-cause contributor (common part number / common software) to G-040; confirm standby-instrument independence closes the residual.

cmaData.subject: Both data network channels — independence of the dual redundant network (G-041)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two data network channels. The two data network channels fail independently, so loss of both requires two independent failures (AND).
cmaData.findings: Installation Design (routing/co-location): the two network channels are stated routed on opposite sides and 'share no connector or penetration' [Effect: supports the AND | Mitigating: physical separation asserted throughout]. However both routes transit the same zones 120/200/300/400/800 (Data network channels 1 and 2 routing), so a zonal event spanning a shared zone — notably the mid-hold crossover zone 300 — could strike both [Effect: defeats the AND for a localised hazard | Mitigating: opposite-side separation within each zone]. Development/Design: the two channels are a common deterministic-network design/protocol — a common protocol or timing defect is common-mode [Effect: common-mode of both channels | Mitigating: none stated; dissimilarity not claimed for the network]. Common Resource (electrical): network channels draw electrical supply — common supply loss not enumerated. Excluded: manufacturing/maintenance not credible drivers given the explicit separation claim.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain the connector/penetration separation as the physical independence basis; add a common-cause contributor for common network design/protocol under G-041 and confirm no shared zonal hazard (zone 300 crossover) fails both. Reconcile against ZSA for zone 300.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two data network channels shall share no connector, penetration, or electrical supply that defeats their independence.
• Common network design/protocol defects shall be shown not to fail both channels simultaneously.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the 'no shared connector or penetration' claim as-built, verify no single zonal event (esp. zone 300) takes both channels, and add a common-design contributor to G-041.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two data network channels
aiRequirements: The two data network channels shall share no connector, penetration, or electrical supply that defeats their independence.
Common network design/protocol defects shall be shown not to fail both channels simultaneously.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the 'no shared connector or penetration' claim as-built, verify no single zonal event (esp. zone 300) takes both channels, and add a common-design contributor to G-041.

cmaData.subject: Three ADIRUs to primary displays — independence of the air/inertial data set (G-042)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three air data inertial reference units. The three ADIRUs fail independently, so loss of air/inertial data to primary displays requires all three to fail (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (electrical): supply is only partially diverse — 'Two are supplied from the main buses and one from the DC essential bus'; the two main-bus ADIRUs share a supply class, so a main-bus event fails two of three [Effect: degrades the AND to effectively the remaining essential-bus unit | Mitigating: one unit on DC essential provides supply diversity for one leg only]. Common Resource (sensors): ADIRUs draw on pitot/static/AoA sensing — a common external air-data source error (icing, blockage) is common-mode across units regardless of internal independence [Effect: correlated erroneous/lost data across the set | Mitigating: separate ports assumed but not enumerated]. Development/Design: three ADIRUs are a common type/part number and common software — a common-mode ADIRU error defeats the redundancy (this exact contributor already appears on the tree at node 95, 'Common-mode ADIRU error (common part…)') [Effect: common-mode of all three | Mitigating: none stated; no dissimilarity claimed]. Installation: units co-located within equipment bays — zonal exposure. Excluded: manufacturing lot folded into common part-number/design.
cmaData.mitigation:
Treat the ADIRU set as identical active redundant components (NASA-FTH rule of thumb) and carry an explicit common-cause contributor under G-042; the two-on-main / one-on-essential split gives only partial supply diversity. Because DAL 'A' is allocated on this page, verify the ADIRU independence principle before crediting any DAL reduction resting on the triplex.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The three ADIRUs shall not share a single air-data sensing source such that a common external error fails the set.
• A common-cause ADIRU contributor (common type/software) shall be included in G-042 and shall not, alone, defeat the triplex independence.
• Supply diversity across the three ADIRUs shall be verified given two share the main-bus class.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to add/confirm the common-part-number ADIRU common-cause contributor on G-042, verify air-data sensing diversity, and confirm the main-bus/essential-bus split does not allow one supply event to take two of three.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three air data inertial reference units
aiRequirements: The three ADIRUs shall not share a single air-data sensing source such that a common external error fails the set.
A common-cause ADIRU contributor (common type/software) shall be included in G-042 and shall not, alone, defeat the triplex independence.
Supply diversity across the three ADIRUs shall be verified given two share the main-bus class.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to add/confirm the common-part-number ADIRU common-cause contributor on G-042, verify air-data sensing diversity, and confirm the main-bus/essential-bus split does not allow one supply event to take two of three.

cmaData.subject: G-043 · Loss of electrical supply to primary display path (Complete loss of flight and navigation information display)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two electrical supply paths feeding the primary display path.. The main AC/DC supply to primary displays and the essential supply to primary displays fail independently (AND gate, nodes 118 and 119 under node 117).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / EPS — Both supply paths are generated, converted and distributed by the single Electrical Power System (EPS): four generators, four TRUs, two DC buses and a DC essential bus derive from a common architecture, and the DC essential bus is described as 'the aircraft's final electrical resort'. A loss propagating through EPS bus-tie/control logic (two bus power control units) could affect both the main and essential feeds — the essential path is not sourced from a physically disjoint power system. Common Resource / EWS routing — Both feeds are carried by the EWS; primary display feeders and the essential supply route must be checked for shared bundle/penetration in the forward fuselage (zones 120/130), which is not established as separated in the SDD. Development/Design — bus power control units are stated dissimilar between left/right pairs, which mitigates common software/logic error. Installation — forward equipment bay (120) and flight deck (130) house the display path; co-location of both feeder routes in these zones is a candidate installation-design common cause. NOTE: this AND-gate DAL reduction rests on supply independence; if the essential and main feeds share EPS distribution logic or an EWS route, the reduction is not assured.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirement (dev/PSSA): the essential supply to primary displays shall be routed and controlled such that no single EPS distribution/control failure and no single EWS routing event defeats both the main and essential feeds. Verification note (ASA/SSA): confirm feeder separation between main and essential display supplies in zones 120/130 against EWS route assignments; confirm the two bus power control units cannot present a common-mode command loss to both feeds.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm via EPS load/bus analysis and EWS routing records that the main and essential display feeders share no bus-control common-mode and no co-located bundle/penetration.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two electrical supply paths feeding the primary display path.
cmaData.aiVerification: Confirm via EPS load/bus analysis and EWS routing records that the main and essential display feeders share no bus-control common-mode and no co-located bundle/penetration.

cmaData.subject: G-046 · Complete loss of flight and navigation information display (top event, node 99)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the primary display path from the integrated standby instrument.. Loss of all primary flight/navigation display (node 100) and loss of the independent standby instrument (node 120) fail independently (AND gate, node 99).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / electrical — Both branches ultimately reference the DC essential bus: the standby instrument is on the DC essential bus (node 122) and the primary path's essential supply (node 119) is also essential-bus derived; SDD states the standby instrument 'shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays', but node 116 (ADIRU 3) and node 122 both cite DC-essential-bus supply — verify the essential-bus loss is not a shared basic event across both branches. Development/Design — the standby is an independent integrated instrument with its own sensing, mitigating common ADIRU/display-processor and common-software error. Installation — standby is wired 'directly to the DC essential bus on a route independent of the primary display feeders'; the primary displays, processors and standby all reside in the flight deck / forward-fuselage zones (120/130), so a zonal event (fire, HIRF) striking that region is a candidate installation-design/environment common cause. Common external input — an erroneous common air-data/inertial source can affect displayed information, but this AND concerns total display LOSS, for which sensor commonality is less coupling than the shared essential bus. NOTE: the AND relies on the standby sharing nothing with the primaries; a shared DC-essential-bus dependency, if present, is a common resource that partially defeats it.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirement (dev/PSSA): the standby instrument supply and route shall remain independent of the primary display path such that no single essential-bus condition and no single flight-deck zonal event removes both. Verification note (ASA/SSA): confirm the DC-essential-bus dependency is not a repeated basic event coupling node 120 and node 100; confirm standby routing separation from primary display feeders per §5.11.5; assess flight-deck/forward-fuselage zonal (120/130) and HIRF (§25.1317) exposure to both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm standby-vs-primary independence by tracing DC essential bus events in the tree for a repeated/common basic event, and confirm zonal separation of standby from primary displays in zones 120/130.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the primary display path from the integrated standby instrument.
cmaData.aiVerification: Confirm standby-vs-primary independence by tracing DC essential bus events in the tree for a repeated/common basic event, and confirm zonal separation of standby from primary displays in zones 120/130.

cmaData.subject: G-052 · Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all engines) (top event, node 123)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the four engines' thrust generation.. Loss of thrust on engines 1, 2, 3 and 4 fail independently (AND across nodes 124/128/132/136), with common-cause fuel and FADEC contributors modelled as explicit OR branches (nodes 140, 143).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / Fuel — the cross-feed gallery is a single spanwise run through the wing box and is 'the only path by which fuel from one side reaches an engine on the other'; common fuel contamination and cross-feed/distribution loss could starve all four engines. This is ALREADY represented in the tree (node 140 OR branch: nodes 141 cross-feed gallery, 142 common contamination) — the CMA confirms the coupling is modelled explicitly and not absorbed into the per-engine AND. Zonal/routing — the fuel feed gallery transits zones 510,530,300,540,520 (single spanwise run) — a zonal event in the wing box (300) or a wing-fire could be a shared cause; PRA/particular-risk attention on the gallery is a recorded SDD item. Development/Design — the four FADECs are dual-channel on four different power sources ('no single bus loss can affect more than one engine'), mitigating common electrical loss; but the engine type is a single common model and FADEC software is common across all four — a common design/software or common manufacturing-lot fault is a genuine common cause, represented by node 143 (common-cause FADEC/engine-control). Common Resource / bleed & electrical — generators and EDPs are engine-driven and per-side segregated (services 'not commingled with the opposite side at any point outboard of the wing root'), mitigating shared-power common cause for thrust generation itself. NOTE: the AND's optimistic four-way independence is valid only because the fuel-gallery and FADEC common causes are carried as explicit OR contributors; if either were removed the top-event probability would be grossly underestimated.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirement (dev/PSSA): fuel cross-feed common-cause (contamination, single-gallery loss) and common FADEC/engine-control fault shall remain explicit contributors to the all-engine top event and shall not be absorbed into the per-engine independent logic. Verification note (ASA/SSA): confirm nodes 140–143 are retained as explicit common-cause branches; substantiate FADEC dissimilarity/monitoring adequacy for a common-model engine; carry the single fuel gallery into PRA/ZSA for the wing-box zone (300).
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm the fuel cross-feed and common FADEC branches remain modelled as explicit common-cause OR contributors (nodes 140, 143), and reconcile the single-gallery routing with the PRA on the fuel feed gallery.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the four engines' thrust generation.
cmaData.aiVerification: Confirm the fuel cross-feed and common FADEC branches remain modelled as explicit common-cause OR contributors (nodes 140, 143), and reconcile the single-gallery routing with the PRA on the fuel feed gallery.

cmaData.subject: G-053 — In-flight deployment inhibit defeated (WOW / radio-altimeter agreement), engine 2 reverser
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar in-flight deployment inhibits (WOW discrete vs radio-altimeter agreement).. The weight-on-wheels inhibit and the radio-altimeter agreement inhibit fail independently, so no single cause defeats both in-flight deployment inhibits.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — both inhibits are electrically/data supplied and both consume avionics-sourced signals (AVI supplies air/inertial/nav data to all systems); a common data-network or ADIRU fault could corrupt the radio-altimeter agreement while the WOW discrete is separately sourced from LDG. WOW is a single distributed discrete from LDG feeding many consumers including the reversers, so a stuck/erroneous WOW is a single-point contributor to the WOW inhibit; independence rests on the radio-altimeter inhibit being genuinely dissimilar and separately routed. Installation — dual radio altimeters are installed; both radio-altimeter channels and the data network channels (routes 1 and 2) transit zone 300, the principal routing crossover zone, so a zonal event in 300 is a physical common-cause candidate against the radio-altimeter agreement path.
cmaData.mitigation:
Dissimilar inhibit sources (physical WOW discrete AND radio-altimeter agreement) already provide functional dissimilarity; retain separate sourcing (LDG WOW vs AVI radio-altimeter), require the radio-altimeter agreement to use both radio altimeters on independent data channels, and require the mechanical translating-sleeve lock as a third dissimilar barrier so no single inhibit loss deploys the reverser in flight.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The reverser in-flight deployment inhibit shall require agreement of a weight-on-wheels discrete AND radio-altimeter agreement AND the mechanical translating-sleeve lock, such that no single common cause defeats all three.
• The radio-altimeter agreement inhibit shall be derived from both radio altimeters on independent data channels not shared with the weight-on-wheels source.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar in-flight deployment inhibits (WOW discrete vs radio-altimeter agreement).
aiRequirements: The reverser in-flight deployment inhibit shall require agreement of a weight-on-wheels discrete AND radio-altimeter agreement AND the mechanical translating-sleeve lock, such that no single common cause defeats all three.
The radio-altimeter agreement inhibit shall be derived from both radio altimeters on independent data channels not shared with the weight-on-wheels source.

cmaData.subject: G-055 — In-flight deployment inhibit defeated (WOW / radio-altimeter agreement), engine 3 reverser
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar in-flight deployment inhibits (WOW discrete vs radio-altimeter agreement) on the engine 3 (right inboard) reverser.. The weight-on-wheels inhibit and the radio-altimeter agreement inhibit fail independently for engine 3, so no single cause defeats both in-flight deployment inhibits.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — as G-053: both inhibits consume avionics-sourced data (AVI serves all systems), and WOW is a single distributed LDG discrete feeding all reversers, so the SAME WOW discrete and the SAME radio-altimeter agreement can be common between engine 2 and engine 3 reverser inhibits — a cross-engine common cause that would defeat the inhibit on BOTH inboard reversers simultaneously. Installation — radio-altimeter data and data-network channels transit zone 300 (principal crossover zone); a zonal event there is a physical common-cause candidate against both inboard reverser radio-altimeter inhibits.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain dissimilar sources; require the WOW inhibit and radio-altimeter agreement inhibit to be evaluated per-reverser so a single WOW or radio-altimeter fault cannot simultaneously arm both inboard reversers; retain the mechanical translating-sleeve lock as an independent third barrier per engine.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The engine 3 reverser in-flight deployment inhibit shall require weight-on-wheels AND radio-altimeter agreement AND mechanical translating-sleeve lock, with no single common cause defeating all three.
• The reverser in-flight deployment inhibit logic shall be evaluated independently per reverser so a single weight-on-wheels or radio-altimeter fault cannot arm both inboard reversers.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar in-flight deployment inhibits (WOW discrete vs radio-altimeter agreement) on the engine 3 (right inboard) reverser.
aiRequirements: The engine 3 reverser in-flight deployment inhibit shall require weight-on-wheels AND radio-altimeter agreement AND mechanical translating-sleeve lock, with no single common cause defeating all three.
The reverser in-flight deployment inhibit logic shall be evaluated independently per reverser so a single weight-on-wheels or radio-altimeter fault cannot arm both inboard reversers.

cmaData.subject: G-054 — Uncommanded in-flight deployment, engine 2 reverser (command AND defeated-inhibit AND mechanical lock)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence of the three barriers to uncommanded in-flight deployment on the engine 2 reverser (actuation command / inhibit logic / mechanical sleeve lock).. Uncommanded reverser actuation command, defeat of the in-flight deployment inhibit, and failure of the mechanical translating-sleeve lock fail independently, so no single cause produces in-flight deployment.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — the actuation command path and the inhibit logic may share electrical supply and avionics data (AVI serves all systems); if the same processing/data corruption both generates a spurious actuation command and defeats the inhibit, the command and inhibit legs are not independent. Development/Design — the actuation command electronics and the inhibit logic could share a common controller or common software, which would defeat the command↔inhibit AND; the mechanical translating-sleeve lock is dissimilar (mechanical) and is the diverse barrier that preserves the AND. Environment — engine 2 reverser hardware, actuation, sleeve lock and nacelle wiring are co-located in nacelle zone 620 (high energy, fire zone); a nacelle fire/overheat/vibration event is a physical common-cause candidate against the actuation and the mechanical lock together.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain the mechanical translating-sleeve lock as a dissimilar, mechanically diverse third barrier independent of the electrical command and inhibit logic; require the actuation command path and the inhibit logic to be segregated (independent power/data or dissimilar processing) so a single electronic fault cannot both command actuation and defeat the inhibit; address nacelle-620 co-location under the engine fire zone / ZSA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The reverser actuation command path and the in-flight deployment inhibit logic shall be segregated such that no single electrical or software fault both commands actuation and defeats the inhibit.
• The mechanical translating-sleeve lock shall remain an independent mechanical barrier not defeated by any fault affecting the actuation command or the inhibit logic.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence of the three barriers to uncommanded in-flight deployment on the engine 2 reverser (actuation command / inhibit logic / mechanical sleeve lock).
aiRequirements: The reverser actuation command path and the in-flight deployment inhibit logic shall be segregated such that no single electrical or software fault both commands actuation and defeats the inhibit.
The mechanical translating-sleeve lock shall remain an independent mechanical barrier not defeated by any fault affecting the actuation command or the inhibit logic.

cmaData.subject: In-flight reverser inhibit independence — engine 3 (FTA gate id 151, AND of command 152 / inhibit-defeated 153 / mechanical lock 156)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the reverser actuation command path, the weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter inhibit logic, and the mechanical translating-sleeve lock.. A spurious reverser deploy command, both electronic in-flight inhibits defeated, and the mechanical translating-sleeve lock failure are independent and must coincide.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source | Effect on Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: [Common Resources — sensing source] WoW and radio-altimeter inhibits (154,155) may derive from common ground/air determination; a single erroneous air-mode source could defeat both electronic inhibits at once, collapsing gate 153 to a single cause | SDD: WoW distributed to many consumers 'including the thrust reversers'; RA agreement is a second, dissimilar inhibit — dissimilarity is the mitigation, must confirm sources are truly independent. :: [Installation/Environment — co-location] Reverser command electronics (152) and inhibit electronics (153) sit in engine 3 nacelle zone 630, a high-energy / flammable-fluid fire zone; a local nacelle event could couple command and inhibit-defeat | Mechanical sleeve lock (156) is outside the electronic chain and provides a dissimilar barrier; local zonal threat still to be reconciled with ZSA/PRA for zone 630 (rotor-burst/engine-burst applicable). :: [Development/Design — common inhibit logic] Both inhibit legs and the deploy command may share reverser controller software/hardware | dissimilar WoW vs RA sensing intended; controller commonality not decomposed in SDD.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm WoW and radio-altimeter inhibit signals derive from independent, dissimilar sources with no shared air/ground determination; verify reverser command path and inhibit path do not share a single controller/power feed; retain mechanical translating-sleeve lock as an independent dissimilar barrier; reconcile nacelle zone 630 co-location against the ZSA and the rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The reverser in-flight deployment inhibit shall use weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter signals derived from independent, dissimilar sources such that no single erroneous air/ground determination defeats both inhibits.
• The reverser actuation command path and the in-flight inhibit path shall not share a single controller, power feed, or nacelle installation route such that a single common cause defeats both.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the reverser actuation command path, the weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter inhibit logic, and the mechanical translating-sleeve lock.
aiRequirements: The reverser in-flight deployment inhibit shall use weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter signals derived from independent, dissimilar sources such that no single erroneous air/ground determination defeats both inhibits.
The reverser actuation command path and the in-flight inhibit path shall not share a single controller, power feed, or nacelle installation route such that a single common cause defeats both.

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the uncommanded thrust increase from engine parameter indications and the resulting yaw/pitch cues, identify the affected engine, and counter with rudder and pitch input while commanding the fuel shut-off and fire handle to isolate it.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-001 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the thrust deficit from engine parameter indications and asymmetry cues, identify the affected engine, and counter the asymmetry while managing the flight path.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-002 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the mismatch between thrust indication and lever position by cross-checking the two, identify that thrust is not tracking the command, and manage thrust manually.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-003 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to carry the additional monitoring load of an unannunciated gradual thrust erosion, recognising it only at a later cue such as a performance shortfall or thrust imbalance, with no discrete action credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-004 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the symmetric performance shortfall from engine and performance indications, assess climb/obstacle capability, and adjust the flight profile or plan a diversion.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-005 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the asymmetry from engine parameters and yaw cues, identify the affected engine, and apply rudder and retrim while managing thrust to continue to a suitable aerodrome.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-006 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to be unaware of the slow asymmetric thrust drift, which sits below the detection threshold, and to carry the associated monitoring load with no corrective action credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-007 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the total loss of thrust from engine indications, identify it as an all-engine failure, and execute a forced-landing procedure with essential control preserved by the automatic RAT deployment.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-008 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the sudden yaw and asymmetry from motion cues and engine indications, identify an in-flight reverser deployment, and apply corrective rudder and thrust management.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-009 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the failure of the reverser to stow from reverser-status indication and residual asymmetry, reduce the affected engine to idle, and continue deceleration on wheel braking.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-010 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the reduced deceleration from rollout progress cues and apply increased wheel braking to compensate.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-011 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the yaw from motion cues, identify asymmetric reverse thrust, and apply steering and differential-braking correction during rollout.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-012 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the absence of reverse-thrust deceleration from rollout cues and rely on wheel braking and autobrake, with elevated attention to stopping distance.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-013 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the erroneous pitch response by comparing aircraft response to inceptor command and attitude indications, identify the erroneous behaviour, and override or reconfigure to a degraded control law or mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-014 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the uncommanded pitch motion from attitude indications and motion cues, identify it as uncommanded, and arrest it via inceptor input, degraded law, or mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-015 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the erroneous roll response by comparing aircraft response to inceptor command and attitude indications, identify the erroneous behaviour, and counter it with inceptor input.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-016 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the uncommanded roll from attitude indications and motion cues, identify it as uncommanded, and counter it with inceptor input, noting no roll reversion path exists if all computers are lost.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-017 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the erroneous yaw response by comparing aircraft response to inceptor command and heading/sideslip indications, identify the erroneous behaviour, and counter it, with lower-segment mechanical reversion available.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-018 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the uncommanded yaw from heading/sideslip indications and motion cues, identify it as uncommanded, and counter it, with lower-segment mechanical reversion available.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-019 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to be unaware of the slow uncommanded roll drift, which sits below the detection threshold and produces no annunciation, and to carry the associated monitoring load until it manifests as a gross attitude change.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-021 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to be unaware of the slow uncommanded yaw drift, which sits below the detection threshold and produces no annunciation, and to carry the associated monitoring load until it manifests as a gross heading/sideslip change.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-022 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to be unaware of the steady surface bias, which produces no discrete indication, and to carry the associated monitoring and trim-compensation load without recognising the hidden offset.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-023 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded control law from its annunciation and to carry the additional flying and procedural load while remaining within controllable limits.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-024 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the controllability situation from control response and attitude cues and to carry the elevated flying load, with the analysis claiming the required workload and precision may exceed what can be sustained in critical take-off/landing phases.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-025 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded pitch capability from the annunciated degraded law and to carry the additional load of maintaining pitch attitude and trim.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-026 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded roll capability from the annunciated degraded law and to carry the additional load of maintaining lateral control and coordinating turns.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-027 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to recognise the degraded yaw capability from the annunciated degraded law and to carry the additional load of holding heading and countering any asymmetric thrust.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-028 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to be unable to maintain controlled flight, with only degraded mechanical reversion available and no recovery credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-029 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the mismatch between high-lift position and selection from position indication and annunciated asymmetry/jam discretes, identify the configuration state, and manage the configuration with performance recomputation.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-030 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: The crew is assumed to detect the uncommanded high-lift movement from position indication and motion cues, diagnose the configuration state, and counter any asymmetry while managing a critical low-altitude phase.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-031 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition
